sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: This study evaluated the performance of liver and spleen stiffness measurement (LSM and SSM) by two-dimensional shear-wave elastography (2D-SWE) in ruling out high-risk esophageal varices (HRVs) and their utility in predicting other portal hypertension-related gastroduodenal lesions and liver-related events (LREs) in patients with cirrhosis.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive adult patients with cirrhosis undergoing screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) between 2023 and 2025 at Chulalongkorn University Hospital, Thailand. LSM and SSM were acquired using 2D-SWE (Supersonic Mach 30) within 2 days of EGD by a single blinded operator. HRVs were defined endoscopically as medium-to-large varices or small varices with red wale markings.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: 169 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled. Of these, 77 (45.6%) and 40 (23.7%) patients had esophageal varices (EVs) and HRVs, respectively. Leading cirrhosis causes were hepatitis B and C virus (n = 66, 39.1%). At thresholds to maximize specificity while maintaining sensitivity ≥ 90%, LSM < 13.7 kPa and SSM < 37.6 kPa by 2D-SWE could spare EGD in 36.7% and 44.4%, respectively, with corresponding missed HRV rates of 4.8% and 4%. Moreover, 2D-SWE-derived LSM and SSM yielded AUCs of 0.778 and 0.844 for HRVs, 0.742 and 0.785 for EVs, and 0.766 and 0.724 for portal hypertensive gastropathy (all p < 0.001). In multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis, Child-Pugh score and LSM by 2D-SWE were independently associated with the development of LREs within 1 year.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: LSM and SSM using 2D-SWE may help reduce the need for screening EGD in patients with cirrhosis, with observed missed-HRV rates of 4.8% and 4.0%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of 2D-SWE for variceal risk stratification, particularly where vibration-controlled transient elastography is unavailable. The proposed cutoffs require external validation before clinical implementation.

items.title: Beyond specificity: growing evidence from validation of CEUS LI-RADS v2017 and proposed revisions.
items.authors: Zhu M, Zhu Z, Liang X, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (CEUS LI-RADS) version 2017 provides a standardized framework for characterizing focal liver observations in patients at high risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although the system has demonstrated clinical utility and is endorsed by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases, accumulating validation evidence reveals an existing gap that limits the application of CEUS LI‑RADS to liver observations beyond those categorized as CEUS LR‑5 for HCC.

sections.text: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (CEUS LI-RADS) version 2017 provides a standardized framework for characterizing focal liver observations in patients at high risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although the system has demonstrated clinical utility and is endorsed by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases, accumulating validation evidence reveals an existing gap that limits the application of CEUS LI‑RADS to liver observations beyond those categorized as CEUS LR‑5 for HCC. This limitation arises mainly from the specificity‑prioritized design of CEUS LR‑5 for HCC, which comes at the cost of sensitivity. In this review, we summarize a group of studies on CEUS LI‑RADS for liver observations, addressing their merits, limitations, and proposals for revision. The proposed modifications are investigational, and have not been incorporated into current guidelines. Our objectives are to reduce misclassification, improve the sensitivity of CEUS LR-5 for HCC while maintaining reasonably high specificity, expand the utility of CEUS LI-RADS to a broader range of liver observations, and ultimately optimize patient management. The 60-s threshold for early washout onset lacks statistical derivation and leads to substantial misclassification of HCC as LR-M (probably or definitely malignant, not necessarily HCC); reported HCC proportions among LR-M lesions range from 41.8% to 86.7%. The definitions of washout degrees (mild vs. marked) are somewhat ambiguous, which cause inter-reader variability, and the absence of objective quantitative metrics. Current discussions regarding potential modification of CEUS LI-RADS v2017 include: (1) shortening the early washout threshold from 60 to < 45 s or other threshold, which markedly improves sensitivity of CEUS LR 5 for HCC with minimal loss of specificity; (2) redefining marked washout as occurring at 3 min or later as an adjunctive criterion; (3) incorporating Kupffer-phase findings when using perfluorobutane (Sonazoid); (4) integrating ancillary features; and (5) considering size-stratified thresholds.

items.title: Histotripsy versus Established Thermal Ablation Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of FDA MAUDE Adverse Event Reporting Patterns.
items.authors: Kundu A, Tam A, Zhao L, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: A sensitivity analysis excluding malfunction-only reports showed similar organ system reporting patterns. Conclusion Histotripsy demonstrated higher reported frequencies of serious AEs and death in early postmarket MAUDE surveillance compared with pooled MWA/RFA; however, differences in technology maturity and reporting era may have contributed to differential AE reporting, warranting prospective evaluation.

sections.text: Background Histotripsy recently received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance for liver tumors, but long-term safety data remain limited. Purpose To characterize histotripsy-related adverse events (AEs) reported to the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database during the early postmarket period and contextualize findings in comparison to microwave ablation (MWA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) during comparable observation windows. Materials and Methods A retrospective analysis of the FDA MAUDE database was conducted. AE reports were analyzed over comparable 24-month postmarket periods: July 2024 to July 2026 for histotripsy, January 2017 to January 2019 for MWA, and January 2016 to January 2018 for RFA. Reports were classified by severity (malfunction, serious injury, and death) and medical problem category. Firth-penalized reporting odds ratios (RORs), relative risks (RRs), and Bayesian modeling using Bass model-derived procedure volumes enabled exploratory denominator-adjusted comparisons. Results Of 570 AE reports initially identified, 506 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final analysis (71 histotripsy [median patient age, 68 years; IQR, 56-76 years] and 435 MWA/RFA [median patient age, 58 years; IQR, 50-67 years]). Serious injury and death occurred in 86% (61 of 71) and 14% (10 of 71) of histotripsy reports versus 20% (89 of 435) and 2% (eight of 435) of MWA/RFA reports. Histotripsy had higher reported odds of serious injury (ROR, 14.24 [95% CI: 6.29, 35.56]; P < .001) and death (ROR, 4.35 [95% CI: 1.08, 24.35]; P = .04). In exploratory analyses using modeled procedure volumes, estimated RRs based on reported events were 6.11 (95% CI: 2.64, 14.11; P < .001) for serious injury and 10.94 (95% CI: 4.73, 25.33; P < .001) for death. Although sparse event counts produced imprecise estimates for some complication categories, histotripsy showed higher reporting odds of renal and urinary complications (P < .001), hemorrhage and vascular injury (P < .001), and gastrointestinal and/or abdominal complications (P < .001) in the full cohort. A sensitivity analysis excluding malfunction-only reports showed similar organ system reporting patterns. Conclusion Histotripsy demonstrated higher reported frequencies of serious AEs and death in early postmarket MAUDE surveillance compared with pooled MWA/RFA; however, differences in technology maturity and reporting era may have contributed to differential AE reporting, warranting prospective evaluation.

items.title: When US and MRI disagree: association of pre- high-intensity focused ultrasound imaging discordance with technical, safety, and clinical outcomes in uterine fibroid ablation.
items.authors: Mohebbi A, Mirza-Aghazadeh-Attari M, Moradi Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In this study, pre-HIFU US-MRI discordance was not associated with clear differences in technical success, technical efficacy, adverse events, or short-term procedural outcomes. Recognition of discordance may still help inform procedural planning and patient counseling within SIR-standardized frameworks.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To evaluate the prevalence of pre-procedural US-MRI discordance and its association with Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR)-standardized outcomes in patients undergoing US-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation for symptomatic uterine fibroids.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: 308 consecutive patients were included. Discordance was defined as mismatch in fibroid type, location, uterine position, or absolute volume percentage difference > 50%. Patients were stratified into concordant (n = 252) and discordant (n = 56) groups. Outcomes were assessed according to SIR domains: technical success (non-perfused volume ratio on day-1 contrast-enhanced MRI), technical efficacy (through six procedural surrogates as a whole: energy-efficiency factor, overall treatment time, cumulative sonication time, treatment intensity, average sonication power, and oxytocin dose), adverse events (SIR classification), and favorable short-term procedural outcome.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Discordance occurred in 18.2% of cases. Categorical agreement was high, with Gwet's AC1 > 0.93, and volume agreement was good, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.773. Day-1 non-perfused volume ratio and technical-success thresholds were comparable between groups. In unadjusted analysis, the energy-efficiency factor was higher after discordant imaging (p = 0.024) and oxytocin use was shifted toward the 60 IU dose (p = 0.036). After adjustment, neither association remained significant (p = 0.191 and 0.228). Adverse-event profiles and the favorable short-term procedural outcome did not differ significantly.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: In this study, pre-HIFU US-MRI discordance was not associated with clear differences in technical success, technical efficacy, adverse events, or short-term procedural outcomes. Recognition of discordance may still help inform procedural planning and patient counseling within SIR-standardized frameworks.

items.title: Exploring clinical variables and interventions to optimize utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding: a retrospective cohort study.
items.authors: Stumetz K, Cash H, Carballeira R, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Multiphase CT-GIB volumes increased exponentially while positive yields remained low. This study demonstrates associations between CT-GIB findings and subsequent treatment pathways and lays the foundation for prospective studies aimed at determining whether interventional pathway-specific imaging selection can be applied without compromising clinical safety.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: Utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding (CT-GIB) has experienced widespread growth in recent years, yet meaningful clinical outcomes associated with increased utilization remain uncertain. This study examines the overall positivity rate for CT-GIB, evaluates variables associated with a positive scan, and assesses the relationship between a positive CT-GIB and subsequent clinical interventions.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: IRB approved retrospective analysis of 1,040 consecutive patients undergoing CT-GIB (Jan. 2019-Mar. 2025). Demographic (age, gender), hemodynamic (heart rate, blood pressure, shock index), laboratory (hemoglobin, platelets, INR, PT/P TT, albumin, BUN, creatinine) and clinical (anticoagulant use, hypertension, malignancy, cirrhosis) parameters were extracted from the electronic medical record within the 48-h periprocedural window. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify variables independently associated with three outcomes: a positive multiphase CT-GIB scan, endovascular intervention within 48 h, and endoscopic intervention within 48 h.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Imaging volume increased 1,044% over the 6.25-year period. Active bleeding was detected in 143/1,040 (13.8%) of CT-GIB. Fourteen patients died within 48 h and were excluded from intervention analysis. Of the remaining positive cohort, 31/141 (22.0%), reflecting the cohort of 141 patients who survived the initial 48-h periprocedural window (i.e., after exclusion of 2 CTGIB+ patients who died within 48 h), underwent acute interventions within 48 h. Angiography was performed alone in 21/141 (14.9%), endoscopic intervention alone in 8/141 (5.7%), and both interventions were performed in 2/141 (1.4%). Variables independently associated with a positive multiphase CT-GIB: age > 65 years (OR = 2.15, 95% CI 1.41-3.30), male sex (OR = 1.54, 95% CI 1.06-2.22), and a nadir systolic BP < 105 mmHg (OR = 3.12, 95% CI 1.47-6.63). A positive multiphase CT-GIB was strongly associated with endovascular intervention (OR = 42.83, 95% CI 14.56-126.01; p < 0.001), but not with endoscopic intervention (OR = 1.53, 95% CI 0.73-3.23; p = 0.261).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Multiphase CT-GIB volumes increased exponentially while positive yields remained low. This study demonstrates associations between CT-GIB findings and subsequent treatment pathways and lays the foundation for prospective studies aimed at determining whether interventional pathway-specific imaging selection can be applied without compromising clinical safety.

items.title: Noninvasive imaging biomarkers of chronic liver disease severity and prognosis.
items.authors: Taktak YB, Gultekin B, Tasci ME, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Our findings suggest that MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers, particularly FLIS, may provide noninvasive imaging markers of disease severity and prognosis in patients with CLD. Prospective studies with long-term clinical outcomes are needed to define their role in risk stratification and transplant decision-making.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To evaluate whether MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers are associated with clinical severity and prognosis in chronic liver disease (CLD).

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: In this retrospective single-center study, 165 adults with chronic liver disease (CLD) who underwent gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI were included. Functional Liver Imaging Score (FLIS) was assessed on 20-min hepatobiliary-phase images, and Liver Surface Nodularity (LSN) was measured on contrast-enhanced axial T1-weighted images using semi-automated software. Spearman correlation analysis was performed for associations with Model for End-Stage Liver Disease 3.0 (MELD 3.0), and Albumin-Bilirubin score (ALBI). Time-to-event analyses for liver transplantation or death within 4 years were performed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the performance of FLIS for predicting 1-year transplant-free survival (TFS).

sections.label: Results
sections.text: FLIS showed moderate inverse correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = - 0.532, p < 0.001) and ALBI score (ρ = - 0.541, p < 0.001). LSN showed weak positive correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = 0.154, p = 0.049) and ALBI score (ρ = 0.184, p = 0.018). In univariable Cox analysis, older age, lower FLIS, higher MELD 3.0, higher ALBI score, and LSN cutoff ≥ 3 were associated with a higher risk of liver transplantation/death. In multivariable analysis, age (hazard ratio (HR), 1.05; p < 0.001), MELD 3.0 (HR, 1.08; p = 0.003) and FLIS group (0-3 vs 4-6 points; HR, 2.39; p = 0.007) remained independently associated with liver transplantation or death. For 1-year TFS, FLIS with an optimal cutoff of ≤ 3 yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.71 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.82).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Our findings suggest that MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers, particularly FLIS, may provide noninvasive imaging markers of disease severity and prognosis in patients with CLD. Prospective studies with long-term clinical outcomes are needed to define their role in risk stratification and transplant decision-making.

items.title: MRI criteria for adenomyosis: interobserver reproducibility of diagnostic features.
items.authors: Villanueva Campos A, Canales Lachén E, Salgado-Parente A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Reproducibility varied widely across MRI features of adenomyosis, and the intermediate levels of the diagnostic certainty scale were not applied consistently. These findings argue for redefining the current MRI criteria for adenomyosis.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To determine which MRI features used in the diagnosis of adenomyosis are reproducible between readers, and whether a diagnostic certainty scale used in routine reporting can be applied consistently.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: Prospective single-center study of 108 consecutive women referred for 3-T pelvic MRI after transvaginal ultrasound suspicion of adenomyosis. Three subspecialized radiologists, with 10, 8 and 5 years of experience, independently assessed all examinations, blinded to clinical data, ultrasound findings and to each other. Diagnostic certainty was recorded on a four-level ordinal scale (definite, probable, possible, absent). Agreement was quantified with Fleiss' kappa for the three readers, Cohen's kappa for pairs, and weighted kappa for ordinal variables.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Agreement for the four-level scale was fair when unweighted (κ = 0.401) and substantial when quadratic-weighted (mean 0.663). No patient was rated probable by all three readers, and agreement across the definite-versus-probable boundary was null (κ = -0.013 to 0.143); collapsing the two categories raised it to κ = 0.581-0.698. For the two direct criteria it was substantial for myometrial hemorrhagic foci (κ = 0.650) and moderate for myometrial cysts (κ = 0.555). Among junctional zone measurements, agreement was moderate for thickness > 12 mm (κ = 0.530) but absent for junctional zone irregularity (κ = 0.048), which was non-evaluable in 21 of 108 examinations (19.4%). These examinations showed a higher prevalence of motion artifacts (p = 0.0005). Agreement on severity grade was moderate (κ = 0.441).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Reproducibility varied widely across MRI features of adenomyosis, and the intermediate levels of the diagnostic certainty scale were not applied consistently. These findings argue for redefining the current MRI criteria for adenomyosis.

items.title: Delayed hepatobiliary phase imaging improves bile leak detection on gadoxetate-enhanced MRI.
items.authors: Vanzulli A, Grégory J, Sartoris R, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Delayed HBP improved bile leak detection without loss of specificity.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Does extending gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase MRI acquisitions beyond the conventional 20-min window improve the detection of active bile leaks? Findings Delayed hepatobiliary-phase imaging raised sensitivity for bile leak detection from 27% to 82% without loss of specificity, highlighting acquisition timing as a key diagnostic determinant. Clinical relevance Delayed gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase imaging is an effective adjunct for detecting active bile leaks and should be considered when findings at conventional timing are negative or equivocal, with direct implications for clinical management.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To compare conventional and delayed (≥ 30 min) hepatobiliary-phase (HBP) gadoxetate-enhanced MRI for the detection of bile leaks.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This retrospective single-center study included all consecutive gadoxetate-enhanced MRI examinations comprising delayed HBP acquisitions performed for suspected biliary leak over 2 years at a tertiary hepatobiliary referral center. Two abdominal radiologists blinded to clinical records independently assessed leak presence at each timepoint. A composite reference standard incorporating endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, surgical exploration, percutaneous drainage findings, and multidisciplinary assessment was utilized to assign ground-truth leak status. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV), accuracy, and inter-reader agreement were calculated.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Thirty-five patients (22 men; median age, 56 years; interquartile range (IQR), 48-65) undergoing 36 examinations were included. The most common indications were liver transplantation (n = 13/35, 37%) and cholecystectomy (n = 11/35, 31%). Conventional and delayed HBP were acquired at a median of 21 and 65 min after injection, respectively. Twenty-two of 36 examinations (61%) were ground-truth positive. Inter-reader agreement was perfect for conventional HBP (κ = 1.00) and excellent for delayed HBP (κ = 0.94; 95% CI 0.84-1.00). Conventional HBP demonstrated 27% sensitivity (95% CI 11-50%), 100% specificity (95% CI 77-100%), and 56% accuracy (95% CI 38-72%). Delayed HBP demonstrated 82% sensitivity (95% CI 60-95%), 100% specificity (95% CI 77-100%), and 89% accuracy (95% CI 74-97%). NPV increased from 47% to 78%. Delayed HBP yielded higher sensitivity and overall accuracy than conventional HBP (p < 0.001, exact McNemar tests).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Delayed HBP improved bile leak detection without loss of specificity.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: Question Does extending gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase MRI acquisitions beyond the conventional 20-min window improve the detection of active bile leaks? Findings Delayed hepatobiliary-phase imaging raised sensitivity for bile leak detection from 27% to 82% without loss of specificity, highlighting acquisition timing as a key diagnostic determinant. Clinical relevance Delayed gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase imaging is an effective adjunct for detecting active bile leaks and should be considered when findings at conventional timing are negative or equivocal, with direct implications for clinical management.

items.title: Three-dimensional automated muscle and adipose analysis to predict hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt.
items.authors: Zhao Y, Huang M, Huang J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Automated 3D muscle and adipose analysis enables objective preprocedural prediction of overt HE after TIPS, which may facilitate clinical decision-making and optimize patient selection.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Can automated three-dimensional muscle and adipose analysis improve reproducible preprocedural prediction of overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt beyond conventional two-dimensional assessment? Findings In 593 patients from seven hospitals, an Integrated Model combining automated three-dimensional body composition and clinical variables outperformed five published clinical comparator scores. Clinical relevance This fully automated three-dimensional body composition (muscle and adipose) analysis enables objective preprocedural risk stratification for overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, supporting more consistent patient selection.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: Overt hepatic encephalopathy (HE) limits the use of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) in portal hypertension. We aimed to determine whether automated three-dimensional (3D) body composition analysis could improve pre-TIPS prediction of overt HE compared with conventional two-dimensional (2D) manual assessment.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This multicenter study included 593 eligible patients from seven institutions (training cohort: n = 308; external validation 1 cohort: n = 151; and external validation 2 cohort: n = 134). After evaluating L3-based 2D measurements, we developed a fully automated 3D muscle and adipose assessment incorporating morphologic and radiomic features. We combined the 3D assessment with selected clinical variables to predict post-TIPS overt HE risk, and benchmarked the final model against published clinical scores. Model performance was evaluated via ROC analysis, DeLong tests, calibration, decision curve analysis, and subgroup analyses.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Traditional 2D measurements showed poor reproducibility, with significant variation in 96.2% (25/26) of features. The 3D Model significantly outperformed the 2D Model. The Integrated Model yielded AUCs of 0.78, 0.73, and 0.77 in the training and two external validation cohorts, exceeding those of Child-Pugh, MELD, ALBI, AMMON-OHE, and Lambda (AUCs 0.47-0.64; all p < 0.05). No significant subgroup differences were observed. High-risk patients had 2- to 4-fold higher overt HE incidence. The model reclassified 40.2% of patients with low pre-TIPS ammonia as high risk and 60.2% of those with high ammonia as low risk.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Automated 3D muscle and adipose analysis enables objective preprocedural prediction of overt HE after TIPS, which may facilitate clinical decision-making and optimize patient selection.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: Question Can automated three-dimensional muscle and adipose analysis improve reproducible preprocedural prediction of overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt beyond conventional two-dimensional assessment? Findings In 593 patients from seven hospitals, an Integrated Model combining automated three-dimensional body composition and clinical variables outperformed five published clinical comparator scores. Clinical relevance This fully automated three-dimensional body composition (muscle and adipose) analysis enables objective preprocedural risk stratification for overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, supporting more consistent patient selection.

items.title: Ultrasound quantification of liver fat in MASLD.
items.authors: Ferraioli G

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently first recognized at ultrasound, but conventional B-mode assessment is limited by subjectivity and reduced sensitivity for mild steatosis. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) techniques address these limitations by converting acoustic signal properties into numerical biomarkers of hepatic fat, including attenuation coefficient, backscatter coefficient, speed of sound, and composite measures.

sections.text: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently first recognized at ultrasound, but conventional B-mode assessment is limited by subjectivity and reduced sensitivity for mild steatosis. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) techniques address these limitations by converting acoustic signal properties into numerical biomarkers of hepatic fat, including attenuation coefficient, backscatter coefficient, speed of sound, and composite measures. This review summarizes the technical principles, current evidence, clinical implementation, and limitations of ultrasound-based liver fat quantification techniques in MASLD. Their major advantages are accessibility, integration into routine ultrasound examinations, and potential use alongside elastography for multiparametric assessment. However, thresholds vary across vendors, software implementations, acquisition protocols, reference standards, and patient populations, limiting interchangeability and universal cutoffs. In clinical practice, ultrasound fat quantification should not be interpreted in isolation but integrated with fibrosis risk stratification and metabolic risk assessment. Further multicenter studies are needed to standardize acquisition and reporting, define clinically meaningful longitudinal changes, and link ultrasound-derived fat reduction with patient outcomes. QUS is therefore best regarded as an evolving, practical framework for objective steatosis assessment that complements, rather than replaces, comprehensive MASLD risk stratification. KEY POINTS: Question Conventional B-mode ultrasound is subjective and insensitive to mild hepatic steatosis, creating an unmet need for objective, reproducible liver fat quantification in MASLD. Findings Attenuation-based and composite quantitative ultrasound methods provide objective liver fat assessment, but vendor-dependent thresholds currently limit interchangeability and universal clinical application. Clinical relevance Quantitative ultrasound enables accessible, objective liver fat assessment during routine imaging, improving detection and grading of hepatic steatosis and supporting risk-based MASLD care; however, vendor-specific thresholds and acquisition variability require technique-specific interpretation.

items.title: A nomogram integrating clinical and radiological data to predict long-term infliximab efficacy in Crohn's disease.
items.authors: Shi X, Chen X, Rao S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The feasible nomogram combining ESR postinduction and SBWT-max at baseline effectively predicts long-term efficacy of IFX, which guides the therapy for CD patients.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: QuestionLoss of response to infliximab is common in Crohn's disease, yet a reliable tool to predict long-term efficacy and guide timely therapeutic decisions remains rare. FindingsA nomogram based on LASSO-logistic regression integrating postinduction ESR and baseline maximum small bowel wall thickness accurately predicted long-term loss of response, including complicated failure. Clinical relevanceThis validated nomogram enables early, risk-stratified identification of patients likely to develop uncomplicated versus complicated loss of response, guiding proactive therapy switch and personalized management in Crohn's disease.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: Infliximab (IFX) is a monoclonal antibody to treat Crohn's disease (CD), but loss of response is common. We aimed to develop an effective nomogram to predict long-term outcomes of IFX.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: A retrospective observational study was conducted on CD patients receiving regular IFX. The endpoint was defined as loss of response within 78 weeks, further classified as uncomplicated or complicated. Baseline characteristics, pre- and postinduction clinical indicators, and computed tomography enterography imaging features were collected. Candidate predictors were selected using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression to construct a clinical-radiological nomogram, validated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, decision curve analysis, and calibration plots. Kaplan-Meier analysis evaluated the clinical implications of predictor cut-off values.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The study enrolled 165 patients, with 112 in the training cohort and 53 in the validation cohort. LASSO-logistic regression revealed erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) at week 14 and maximum small bowel wall thickness (SBWT-max) at baseline as independent predictors of long-term non-response. The nomogram achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.834 (training) and 0.913 (validation) for loss of response, and 0.746 and 0.876 for uncomplicated and complicated loss of response, respectively. Validation of the nomogram confirmed its discriminative, calibrating, and clinical utility. Additionally, ESR at week 14 > 10.5 mm/h or baseline SBWT-max > 7.5 mm showed reduced response duration.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: The feasible nomogram combining ESR postinduction and SBWT-max at baseline effectively predicts long-term efficacy of IFX, which guides the therapy for CD patients.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: QuestionLoss of response to infliximab is common in Crohn's disease, yet a reliable tool to predict long-term efficacy and guide timely therapeutic decisions remains rare. Clinical relevanceThis validated nomogram enables early, risk-stratified identification of patients likely to develop uncomplicated versus complicated loss of response, guiding proactive therapy switch and personalized management in Crohn's disease.

items.title: Beyond chronological age: uncovering disease-dependent variability in AI-driven pediatric bone age assessment.
items.authors: Schön F, Meißner C, Spieth S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The investigated algorithm showed good agreement with bone age assessments performed by pediatric radiologists in a large pediatric cohort. Novel to previous studies, the indication for imaging was considered, demonstrating that agreement between algorithm output and radiologists' assessments varied across disease groups, with highest agreement observed in orthopedic indications.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question The performance of artificial intelligence tools for bone age assessment among different subgroups of pediatric patients according to underlying diseases has not yet been investigated. Findings Automated bone age assessment reliably correlates with estimation by pediatric radiologists. Software output differs according to disease groups, with best results for orthopedic indications. Critical relevance statement In a real-world scenario, the commercial software showed good agreement with routine bone age assessments in a large cohort of pediatric patients. The observed disease-dependent variation suggests that radiologists should consider disease-specific differences when using additional automated tools.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To assess performance and agreement of a commercial artificial intelligence (AI) tool relative to routine pediatric radiologists' bone age assessments in a large pediatric cohort, with focus on different groups of growth disorders.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: One thousand five hundred sixteen anterior-posterior hand radiographs of pediatric patients (50.6% boys, mean age 10.84 ± 3.66 years) were retrospectively analyzed using the AI tool BoneAge. AI results were compared with board-certified pediatric radiologists' reports using Bland-Altman plots, Spearman correlations, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Subgroup analyses were performed for three major indications: genetic/neuroendocrine (n = 1179), orthopedic (n = 152), and oncologic disorders (n = 185).

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Mean absolute difference (MAD) in estimated bone age by radiologists and AI was 6.4 ± 7.0 months for the whole cohort, with complete concordance in 45.1% of cases. Best results were achieved in orthopedic questions with an MAD of 4.1 ± 5.6 months (genetic/neuroendocrine: 6.6 ± 7.2, oncologic: 6.7 ± 6.3 months). There was significant correlation between AI and radiologists for the whole study population (ρ = 0.980), and the three main groups: genetic/neuroendocrine (ρ = 0.974), orthopedic (ρ = 0.952), and oncologic indications (ρ = 0.988). ICCs for the entire cohort and the main indication groups were > 0.9, indicating excellent agreement between radiologist and AI.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: The investigated algorithm showed good agreement with bone age assessments performed by pediatric radiologists in a large pediatric cohort. Novel to previous studies, the indication for imaging was considered, demonstrating that agreement between algorithm output and radiologists' assessments varied across disease groups, with highest agreement observed in orthopedic indications.

items.title: Renal Multiparametric MRI for Early Detection and Longitudinal Monitoring of Metabolic Dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Associated Kidney Injury: Histopathologic Validation and Multi-Omics Profiling.
items.journal_full: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
items.authors: Wang Y, Qin J, Yuan H, et al.

conclusion.label: Data conclusion
conclusion.text: Renal mpMRI detected early kidney injury during MASLD progression.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Kidney injury during metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progression remains incompletely characterized.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To assess multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) for early detection and monitoring of MASLD-associated kidney injury.

sections.label: Study type
sections.text: Animal model.

sections.label: Animal model
sections.text: Fifty male Sprague Dawley rats received high-fat diet plus very low-dose carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) underwent mpMRI before sacrifice at 0, 2, 4, 8, or 12 weeks (n = 10/time point). Ten MASLD and ten normal rats underwent serial MRI at each time point; ten CCl4-only rats served as nephrotoxicity controls. Twelve additional healthy rats underwent a scan-rescan test.

sections.label: Field strength/sequence
sections.text: 3 T; turbo spin-echo T2-weighted imaging, variable flip angle (VFA) gradient-echo T1 mapping, multi-echo gradient-echo blood oxygen level-dependent imaging, pulsed arterial spin labeling, echo-planar diffusion kurtosis imaging, and multi-echo Dixon imaging.

sections.label: Assessment
sections.text: Two radiologists (5 and 13 years of experience) quantified T1, T2*, proton density fat fraction (PDFF), mean diffusivity, mean kurtosis (MK), and renal blood flow (RBF) in cortex, outer/inner stripes of outer medulla (OSOM/ISOM). Early injury was defined as a tubular injury score ≥ 2. Histopathology, immunohistochemistry, transcriptomics, and serum metabolomics were performed.

sections.label: Statistical tests
sections.text: Repeated-measures ANOVA; intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). p < 0.05 indicated significance.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Scan-rescan ICCs were 0.682-0.876. OSOM MK/PDFF significantly increased by Week 2 [MK (×10-3): 0.532 ± 0.007 to 0.574 ± 0.004; PDFF (%): 2.489 ± 0.243 to 3.600 ± 0.347]; cortical RBF and OSOM T2* showed no significant changes at Week 2 (p = 0.786, 1.000) but significantly decreased from Week 4. OSOM MK/PDFF had AUCs of 0.952 and 0.905 for early renal injury. Multi-omics revealed inflammatory and lipid/bile acid alterations. Dodecanedioic/hippuric acids potentially linked MASLD severity to OSOM MK.

sections.label: Data conclusion
sections.text: Renal mpMRI detected early kidney injury during MASLD progression.

sections.label: Technical efficacy
sections.text: Stage 2.

items.title: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: a practical imaging approach.
items.authors: de Paiva Guimarães Barreiro T, Lewin F, Cazzo E, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms.

sections.text: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms. Accurate preoperative recognition may have important implications for patient management and surgical planning. This review summarizes the imaging features of c-PanNETs across computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, as well as the complementary roles of endoscopic ultrasound and somatostatin receptor PET/CT. Particular attention is given to arterial hyperenhancement of the cyst wall, septations, mural nodules, or residual solid components; assessment of communication with the main pancreatic duct; and integration of complementary imaging findings. Because these features are not specific, their interpretation in combination with lesion morphology and ductal relationships is emphasized. Practical approaches to differential diagnosis and common interpretive pitfalls are also discussed. The review further addresses emerging quantitative imaging techniques, including radiomics and artificial intelligence, while recognizing that evidence specific to c-PanNETs remains limited. A practical diagnostic algorithm and structured reporting checklist are provided to support systematic interpretation and multidisciplinary communication. Recognition of the imaging spectrum of c-PanNETs, combined with systematic assessment of enhancement characteristics, ductal anatomy, and complementary imaging findings, may improve diagnostic confidence and support appropriate patient management.

items.title: 18F-FDG PET/CT Findings in a Patient With Uterine Adenomyoma.
items.authors: Zhang W, Cai L, Feng Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Histopathologic and immunohistochemical findings revealed uterine adenomyoma. This case suggests that uterine adenomyoma with intense FDG uptake is easily misdiagnosed as malignancy, and diagnosis should be confirmed by pathology.

sections.text: A 50-year-old woman presented to our hospital with lower abdominal pain for 1 week. Pelvic CT revealed a significantly enlarged uterus with multiple nodular and mass lesions. Subsequently, the patient underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT examination.18F-FDG PET/CT revealed multiple nodules and mass lesions in the uterus with intense 18F-FDG uptake. The patient underwent needle biopsy of the uterine lesion. Histopathologic and immunohistochemical findings revealed uterine adenomyoma. This case suggests that uterine adenomyoma with intense FDG uptake is easily misdiagnosed as malignancy, and diagnosis should be confirmed by pathology.

items.title: Atlas-Based Mapping of Hepatic Fat by Sex: Results From the Lifestyle Intervention (LION) Study.
items.journal_full: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
items.authors: Starck S, Junker D, Sideri-Lampretsa V, et al.

conclusion.label: Data conclusion
conclusion.text: Hepatic fat loss showed spatially heterogeneous and sex-specific patterns. Heterogeneity reflected metabolic state cross-sectionally but mainly adiposity change longitudinally.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Hepatic proton density fat fraction (PDFF) is often reported as a whole-liver mean, without a population reference for individual fat distribution.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To construct longitudinal, sex-specific three-dimensional PDFF atlases and assess regional fat loss, sex differences in heterogeneity, and metabolic associations.

sections.label: Study type
sections.text: Prospective; secondary analysis of a randomized lifestyle intervention trial.

sections.label: Population
sections.text: A total of 127 adults with obesity imaged at baseline ( V 1 , 73 female [F], 54 male [M]), after an 8-week low-caloric diet ( V 2 , 49F/32M), and after 12-month weight maintenance ( V 3 , 40F/32M).

sections.label: Field strength/sequence
sections.text: 3T; six-echo chemical shift-encoded gradient-echo.

sections.label: Assessment
sections.text: Sex- and visit-specific atlases were built by deformable registration; z-maps quantified voxel-wise deviation from the matched atlas. Six heterogeneity features (standard deviation [σx], coefficient of variation [CV], entropy [ H ]; z- skewness, z-kurtosis, volume fraction z > 2) were compared between sexes and correlated, cross-sectionally and longitudinally, with hepatocellular, glycemic, adiposity markers and triglycerides, and longitudinally with steatosis remission (PDFF < 5%).

sections.label: Statistical tests
sections.text: Welch t-test; Spearman correlation (ρ); Benjamini-Hochberg correction within each test set. Significance at adjusted p < 0.05.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Liver PDFF decreased significantly from V 1 to V 2 in males (13.6% ± 7.0% to 6.6% ± 2.5%) and females (9.1% ± 6.2% to 5.9% ± 3.3%) with regionally non-uniform, sex-specific patterns. At V 1 , σx and H were significantly higher in males and CV, z-skewness and z-kurtosis in females; at V 2 , σx (males) and z-skewness and z-kurtosis (females) remained significant; no feature differed at V 3 (adjusted p = [0.583-0.953]). Cross-sectionally, features correlated with hepatocellular, glycemic and adiposity markers, more extensively in females. Longitudinally, significant correlations were almost limited to adiposity (V1 to V3: CV × visceral fat volume in females, ρ = -0.65; CV × visceral PDFF in males, ρ = -0.67); apart from H × gamma-glutamyl transferase in females, no feature tracked hepatocellular, glycemic or steatosis remission outcomes (adjusted p = [0.051-0.999], [0.092-0.999], and [0.073-0.887]).

sections.text: Hepatic fat loss showed spatially heterogeneous and sex-specific patterns. Heterogeneity reflected metabolic state cross-sectionally but mainly adiposity change longitudinally.

items.authors: Maino C, Cristoferi L, Carminati R, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: S-FLIS outperformed established morphological MRI/MRCP scores in identifying high-risk PSC patients, and pairing functional (S-FLIS) with morphological (ANALI) assessment yielded the greatest incremental value, supporting a multiparametric non-invasive approach to risk stratification in PSC.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Can an S-FLIS improve non-invasive risk stratification in PSC beyond whole-liver FLIS and established morphological MRI/MRCP scores, alone or in combination? Findings S-FLIS outperformed FLIS, ANALI, and DiStrict as a standalone discriminator of high-risk PSC patients, and its combination with ANALI achieved the highest discriminative accuracy (AUC up to 0.864). sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To assess the reproducibility of a segmental functional liver imaging score (S-FLIS) and whether it improves risk stratification in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) beyond global FLIS (G-FLIS) and established MRI/MRCP-based scores (ANALI, ANALI Gd+, DiStrict), alone or combined.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This prospective study included consecutive adult PSC patients undergoing standardised gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI, blood tests and liver stiffness measurement (LSM). G-FLIS, S-FLIS, DiStrict, ANALI and ANALI Gd+ were computed, and interobserver agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa. Univariate and bivariate logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses evaluated discrimination for two surrogate risk biomarkers: LSM > 9.6 kPa and Mayo risk score (MRS) > 0.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Seventy-seven patients were included (median age 45 years; 62.3% male). Interobserver agreement was almost perfect for DiStrict (κ = 0.98), substantial for G-FLIS (κ = 0.608) and moderate to almost perfect for S-FLIS across hepatic segments (κ = 0.524-0.861). Unlike G-FLIS, S-FLIS was significantly associated with both high LSM and high MRS. Among individual scores, S-FLIS achieved the highest discriminative performance for high LSM (AUC = 0.782) and high MRS (AUC = 0.816), outperforming ANALI (0.668 and 0.702) and DiStrict (0.713 and 0.741). Bivariate models combining ANALI and S-FLIS achieved the highest performance for both endpoints (AUC = 0.843 and 0.864).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: S-FLIS outperformed established morphological MRI/MRCP scores in identifying high-risk PSC patients, and pairing functional (S-FLIS) with morphological (ANALI) assessment yielded the greatest incremental value, supporting a multiparametric non-invasive approach to risk stratification in PSC.

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of Nectin-4-targeted [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT versus [18F]-FDG PET/CT for Staging of Locally Advanced and Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma: A Prospective, Single-center, Phase 2 Feasibility Trial.
items.authors: Laukhtina E, Muin D, Spielvogel CP, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT is feasible for whole-body nectin-4 assessment in la/mUC and supports a distinct biodistribution from FDG, suggesting complementary rather than interchangeable roles. Further prospective evaluation with treatment-outcome correlation is warranted before its use as a biomarker to guide EV-based therapy selection.

sections.text: Enfortumab vedotin (EV), an anti-nectin-4 antibody-drug conjugate, alone and with pembrolizumab (EV plus pembrolizumab [EV/P]), has transformed the treatment of locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC), yet remains biomarker agnostic. We prospectively evaluated [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT ([68Ga]-N188 PET/CT) as a whole-body alternative for nectin-4 imaging, with [18F]-FDG PET/CT as an active comparator and conventional computed tomography as the reference standard for staging la/mUC in 25 patients planned for EV/P. [18F]-FDG PET/CT showed a higher maximum standardized uptake value and tumor-to-background ratio than [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT across most lesion types (primary tumor, visceral, and osseous), except for lymph nodes. The overall tracer correlation was weak (Spearman r = 0.196), strongest in lymph nodes (r = 0.657), and absent in primary tumors and bone lesions. For primary tumor detection, [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT had higher specificity (86% vs 57%) and positive predictive value (92% vs 83%) than FDG, which had higher sensitivity (88% vs 67%). Nodal staging performance was similar in the tracers. For distant metastases, both achieved 100% sensitivity and negative predictive value, with [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT showing marginally higher specificity. [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT is feasible for whole-body nectin-4 assessment in la/mUC and supports a distinct biodistribution from FDG, suggesting complementary rather than interchangeable roles. Further prospective evaluation with treatment-outcome correlation is warranted before its use as a biomarker to guide EV-based therapy selection.

items.title: Total-Body 18F-FAPI PET/CT for Assessment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Pilot Study.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Malige S, Abdelhafez YG, Spencer BA, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Conclusion: Dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET enables quantitative visualization of hepatic fibroblast activation in MASLD. SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval correlates more strongly with fibrosis severity, supporting 18F-FAPI-74 PET as a promising molecular biomarker for assessing and potentially monitoring metabolic fibrosis.

sections.text: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for fibrosis assessment; however, its invasiveness limits its suitability for routine clinical use. The rising prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as a leading cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma underscores the need for reliable noninvasive assessment. Current noninvasive imaging methods provide surrogate measures of fibrosis but do not directly assess fibrogenic activity. In contrast, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables molecular imaging of activated fibroblasts, a key driver of fibrosis. This study evaluates dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET imaging to assess hepatic fibrogenic activity in MASLD. Methods: In this prospective pilot study, 10 subjects (3 healthy volunteers, 4 patients with mild-moderate fibrosis, and 3 patients with advanced fibrosis) underwent 60-min dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET/CT. SUV and blood-normalized SUV ratio (SUVR) were quantified across time frames, and the net influx rate was derived from dynamic data. MR elastography-derived liver stiffness values were obtained for comparison. Correlations with histologic fibrosis scoring of biopsy tissue were assessed using Spearman analysis. Results: At 5 min postinjection, SUVR correlated strongly with histologic fibrosis score (ρ = 0.95; 95% CI, 0.75-1.00; P = 1.89 × 10-5), followed by SUV (ρ = 0.78; 95% CI, 0.23-0.98; P = 0.0077) and net influx rate from kinetic modeling (ρ = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.41-0.98; P = 0.0022). SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval allowed clearer differentiation among healthy volunteers, patients with mild fibrosis, and patients with advanced fibrosis. Conclusion: Dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET enables quantitative visualization of hepatic fibroblast activation in MASLD. SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval correlates more strongly with fibrosis severity, supporting 18F-FAPI-74 PET as a promising molecular biomarker for assessing and potentially monitoring metabolic fibrosis.

items.title: Comparable Daughter Radionuclide Redistribution with Superior Tumor Absorbed Dose of the SSTR2 Antagonist [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 Versus [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Desai P, Chouin N, Huber M, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 achieved a higher TAD and more favorable tumor-to-kidney ratio compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Overall, these findings support further evaluation of antagonist-based 225Ac radiopharmaceutical therapy.

sections.text: It has been hypothesized that effective cellular internalization is required for the retention of 225Ac daughter radionuclides. Both the complex decay chain of 225Ac and the recoil-mediated release of daughters, particularly 213Bi (half-life, 46 min), raise concerns about redistribution that may reduce tumor absorbed dose (TAD) and increase off-target radiation exposure. Because somatostatin receptor subtype 2 antagonists, such as satoreotide tetraxetan (SSO110, also known as DOTA-JR11), are not internalized, it has been proposed that the daughter radionuclides are less effectively retained compared with internalizing agonists, such as DOTATATE. In this study, we performed a direct and quantitative comparison of daughter radionuclide redistribution after administration of [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 and [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Methods: Biodistribution and 213Bi redistribution were evaluated in BALB/c nude mice bearing NCI-H69 small cell lung cancer xenografts. Repeated γ-counting combined with biexponential modeling was used to quantify 225Ac and 213Bi activity in tumors, blood, bone marrow, kidneys, the liver, and the intestines up to 96 h postinjection. TAD was calculated with and without accounting for experimentally derived 213Bi redistribution. Real-time in vitro binding assays were conducted to characterize cellular retention of [225Ac]Ac-SSO110. Results: [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 demonstrated higher tumor uptake and prolonged retention compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution of 213Bi from tumors was minimal and comparable between the agonist and antagonist and reduced the TAD by 4.5% for [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 and 3.9% for [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. After accounting for this redistribution, [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 delivered a 2.8-fold higher TAD and a 1.8-fold higher tumor-to-kidney absorbed dose (AD) ratio compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Moreover, 213Bi redistribution had no relevant impact on AD estimates in evaluated healthy organs, including the kidneys, the intestines, blood, and bone marrow. Real-time binding studies demonstrated a sustained cell-associated β--signal after incubation with [225Ac]Ac-SSO110. Conclusion: Despite negligible internalization, [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 did not show increased macroscopic 213Bi redistribution compared with the internalizing agonist [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution was limited for both radiopeptides and had only a minor effect on AD estimates for tumors and the evaluated healthy tissues. [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 achieved a higher TAD and more favorable tumor-to-kidney ratio compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Overall, these findings support further evaluation of antagonist-based 225Ac radiopharmaceutical therapy.

items.title: A SPECT-Guided, PET-Sparing Algorithm for PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Evaluation (SPARE).
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Kassas M, Zekri M, Poenaru R, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Conclusion: A SPECT-guided algorithm could have avoided most interim PSMA PET studies and reproduced real-world treatment decisions after 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA with high agreement. This algorithm may serve as the basis for a standardized treatment management framework, pending independent, prospective outcome-based validation.

sections.text: [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy is delivered as repeated cycles, yet the decision to continue or adapt treatment after the second cycle is not standardized. Posttherapy SPECT/CT is routinely performed but rarely used formally for response assessment. We developed a multimodality, response-adapted algorithm applied after cycle 2 and tested its concordance with real-world decisions. Methods: We studied 142 men with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer) who completed at least 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA and underwent posttherapy SPECT/CT, baseline and 12-wk prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, and baseline and interim prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET and [18F]FDG PET. Response was assessed in accordance with Prostate Cancer Working Group 4 recommendations for PSA and with RECIP 1.0 for SPECT and PSMA PET. The algorithm combined SPECT/CT and PSA, used PSMA PET only when both were stable, and yielded 3 recommendations: continue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, discontinue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, or consider [18F]FDG PET. The primary endpoints were the number of interim PSMA PET studies avoided and the concordance between algorithm recommendations (continue vs. discontinue) and real-world decisions. The secondary endpoint was intermodality response evaluation concordance. Results: The algorithm recommended continuation in 74 patients (52.1%), discontinuation in 49 patients (34.5%), and [18F]FDG PET in 19 patients (13.4%). Interim PSMA PET/CT could be avoided in 120 patients (84.5%) (95% CI, 77.7%-89.5%). Among patients with a definitive recommendation, conditional agreement of the algorithm with real-world management decisions was 91.1% (95% CI, 84.7%-94.9%), with a κ of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.69-0.91). All 74 patients (100%) with an algorithm recommendation to continue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment continuation, whereas 38 (78%) of 49 patients with an algorithm recommendation to discontinue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment discontinuation. Response classification on SPECT agreed only moderately with PSA level (κ = 0.45) and PSMA PET (κ = 0.47), but the combination of SPECT and PSA raised agreement with PSMA PET to "substantial" (κ = 0.67), approaching that of PSMA PET with PSA level (κ = 0.70). Every discordant decision (n = 11) occurred when the algorithm recommended treatment discontinuation in a patient who nonetheless continued treatment, most commonly because [177Lu]Lu-PSMA was being used as a last line of therapy (7/11, 64%). Conclusion: A SPECT-guided algorithm could have avoided most interim PSMA PET studies and reproduced real-world treatment decisions after 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA with high agreement. This algorithm may serve as the basis for a standardized treatment management framework, pending independent, prospective outcome-based validation.

items.title: PSMA Total Tumor Volume: A Simple Quantifiable Biomarker for Overall Survival Prediction-Results from the International PROMISE PET Registry.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Karpinski MJ, Civan C, Hoberück S, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Conclusion: Among quantifiable PET metrics, PSMA TTV had the highest prognostic accuracy for OS in patients with prostate cancer. Automated PSMA TTV assessment may facilitate fast and reproducible outcome prediction in the future.

sections.text: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET is an accurate prognostic imaging biomarker of survival in patients with prostate cancer when assessed using Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) criteria. Previously, PSMA PET PROMISE risk nomograms were created that surpassed clinical prediction tools. In this study, we focused on the evaluation of quantifiable biomarkers to simplify and facilitate overall survival (OS) prediction. Methods: Data from patients with histologically proven prostate cancer who underwent PSMA PET between December 2012 and April 2024 at participating imaging centers worldwide and who were included in the PROMISE PET Registry by January 31, 2026, were analyzed. Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels at PSMA PET, disease stage, and OS follow-up data were collected. PSMA total tumor volume (PSMA TTV) and whole-body SUVmean were assessed using predefined SUV thresholds. PSMA total lesion uptake (PSMA TL) was calculated as PSMA TTV × SUVmean PSA level at PSMA PET adjusted for PSMA TTV was calculated as PSA × TTV. Univariate regression analysis was conducted to identify potential predictors. Prognostic accuracy of quantitative biomarkers was compared using Harrell C-indices and time-dependent concordance in the development cohort. Probabilities for 3-, 5-, and 7-y OS across PSMA TTV quartiles were derived from Kaplan-Meier curves. Subgroup analysis was conducted by cancer stage. Results: In total, 13,893 patients were included in the analysis and divided 2:1 into development (n = 9271) and validation (n = 4622) cohorts. The prognostic accuracy of PSMA TTV in the validation cohort (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.77-0.80) was superior to SUVmean (C-index, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.61-0.64) and PSA level at PET (C-index, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.69-0.72) and similar to PSMA TL (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.76-0.79) and PSA × TTV (C-index, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.75-0.78). In the entire cohort, the median OS for PSMA TTV quartile 1 (0 mL) and quartile 2 (>0-2.1 mL) was not reached. The median OS was 11.4 y (interquartile range, 10.1 y to not reached) for PSMA TTV quartile 3 (>2.1-16.2 mL) and 4.4 y (interquartile range, 4.2-4.6 y) for quartile 4 (>16.17 mL). Conclusion: Among quantifiable PET metrics, PSMA TTV had the highest prognostic accuracy for OS in patients with prostate cancer. Automated PSMA TTV assessment may facilitate fast and reproducible outcome prediction in the future.

items.title: Test-Retest Repeatability of Peripheral Ganglion Uptake on 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT: Implications for Interpreting Benign Uptake on PSMA PET.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Moin A, Markowski MC, Pienta KJ, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Conclusion: The repeatability of uptake in peripheral ganglia on prostate-specific membrane antigen PET scans is similar to the repeatability of uptake in prostate cancer tumors. As such, isolated changes in uptake cannot be used as de facto evidence of a malignant lesion.

sections.text: Repeatability of uptake in benign structures on prostate-specific membrane antigen PET is unexplored and poorly understood. We used a post hoc analysis of a test-retest cohort to assess repeatability of uptake in peripheral ganglia. Methods: Twenty-two patients were included. Spheric volumes of interest were manually placed on the cervical and lumbosacral dorsal root ganglia, the cervicothoracic ganglia, and the celiac ganglia. Repeatability was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficient, within-subject coefficient of variation, and Bland-Altman limits of agreement. Results: Ganglion uptake demonstrated an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.82 and a within-subject coefficient of variation of 13.1%. Bland-Altman analysis on a relative scale demonstrated that the mean bias was 0.9%, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from -35.8% to 37.6%, broadly comparable to the repeatability of prostate cancer tumors previously reported. Conclusion: The repeatability of uptake in peripheral ganglia on prostate-specific membrane antigen PET scans is similar to the repeatability of uptake in prostate cancer tumors. As such, isolated changes in uptake cannot be used as de facto evidence of a malignant lesion.

items.title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen PET/CT Segmentation Guided by Vision Language Models Embedding Clinical Report Semantics.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Pouromidi M, Bayasi N, Samimi R, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: This approach may reduce manual cleanup and support more reliable quantitative workflows, although precision gains should be weighed against a modest recall reduction. External validation, extension of the true-positive-only analysis to independent cohorts, and PSMA-specific language pretraining are warranted.

sections.text: Whole-body prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT segmentation remains challenging: manual contouring is unsustainable, and image-only artificial intelligence models often misclassify physiologic uptake as malignant, causing high false-positive rates. These limitations underscore the need for segmentation strategies that incorporate the nuclear medicine expertise encoded in PET/CT reports but not used by current models. We investigated whether routine PET/CT reports improve automated lesion segmentation for prostate cancer. Methods: We developed a language-guided 3-dimensional SegResNet fusing report text with 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT image features, encoding report semantics via 4 strategies (BiomedVLP, RadGraph, GPT-raw, GPT-engineered) compared with an image-only model (baseline). Of 320 patients who underwent 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, 297 studies were available; 13 were excluded for missing reports or incomplete image-mask pairs, leaving 284 for analysis, split at the patient level into 243 development cases and a fixed 41-case held-out test set. Metrics included Dice, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, average symmetric surface distance, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance, surface Dice similarity at 5 mm, and lesion-level false positives, using 3 matching criteria (any overlap; 1-to-1 maximum IoU matching, IoU ≥ 0.5; and correct localization of the SUVmax voxel). Significance was assessed using paired 1-sided Wilcoxon tests with Holm adjustment. Results: Report guidance consistently reduced false positives and improved whole-mask boundary agreement. False-positive lesions were reduced by nearly 4 per patient with BiomedVLP and by approximately 3 per patient with RadGraph and GPT-raw. Average symmetric surface distance decreased from 105.4 ± 62.5 mm (image only) to 23.4 ± 18.2 mm with BiomedVLP, 36.9 ± 22.4 mm with RadGraph, and 36.3 ± 26.4 mm with GPT-raw; 95th percentile Hausdorff distance improved from 455.0 ± 169.3 mm to 123.8 ± 80.3 mm with BiomedVLP, and surface Dice similarity at 5 mm increased from 0.638 ± 0.172 to 0.705 ± 0.181. However, when these surface metrics were recomputed on matched true-positive lesions only using the same 3 criteria, no language-guided model differed significantly from the image-only model for any surface metric (all Holm-adjusted P = 1.0), indicating that the whole-mask improvements were attributable to false-positive suppression rather than genuine gains in contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. Precision increased for BiomedVLP (0.099) and RadGraph (0.060), with a modest decrease in voxel-level recall (-0.051, BiomedVLP), reflecting a precision-recall trade-off from suppression of spurious uptake. Dice improved by 0.032 but was borderline significant; IoU increased for BiomedVLP (0.036). Lesion-level sensitivity changed by no more than 0.04 for all models and did not reach significance. Total lesion PSMA remained highly correlated with manual measurements (r ≥ 0.85), whereas PSMA tumor volume correlations were more variable across models (r = 0.37-0.70). Conclusion: The integration of PET/CT report semantics into automated PSMA PET/CT segmentation substantially reduced false-positive lesions and preserved total lesion PSMA agreement with manual measurements; a matched true-positive-only reanalysis indicated that the accompanying whole-mask boundary-agreement gains reflected false-positive suppression rather than improved contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. This approach may reduce manual cleanup and support more reliable quantitative workflows, although precision gains should be weighed against a modest recall reduction. External validation, extension of the true-positive-only analysis to independent cohorts, and PSMA-specific language pretraining are warranted.

items.title: Intense Focal Renal 18F-MFBG Uptake Attributable to Radiation in a Pediatric Patient With Neuroblastoma.
items.authors: Zhang K, Zhang B, Wang Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: No structural renal lesion was identified on cross-sectional imaging, and no evidence of renal tumor was found during 12 months of clinical and imaging follow-up. This case illustrates that intense localized renal 18F-MFBG uptake may result from radiation and should be recognized as a potential pitfall in post-radiotherapy 18F-MFBG PET/CT interpretation.

sections.text: A 9-year-old boy with neuroblastoma was enrolled in a clinical trial. After radiotherapy to the primary tumor site, 18F-MFBG PET/CT was performed 2 months later. No abnormal radiotracer accumulation suggestive of metastatic disease was identified. However, focal intense 18F-MFBG uptake was observed in the upper pole of the left kidney, within the previously irradiated field. No structural renal lesion was identified on cross-sectional imaging, and no evidence of renal tumor was found during 12 months of clinical and imaging follow-up. This case illustrates that intense localized renal 18F-MFBG uptake may result from radiation and should be recognized as a potential pitfall in post-radiotherapy 18F-MFBG PET/CT interpretation.

items.title: Novel Bifunctional PET Tracer 68Ga-DOTA-NI-FAPI-04 PET/CT in Gastrointestinal Tumors: An Exploratory Comparative Study With 18F-FDG.
items.authors: Wang Y, Jin W, Xiang J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: 68Ga-NI-FAPI exhibits superior diagnostic performance in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG, particularly in staging, SRCC evaluation, and metastasis detection. The positive correlation between tumor size and uptake supports its potential for patient selection in ligand-directed radionuclide therapy, establishing it as an effective theranostic agent for gastrointestinal tumors.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: This study aims to evaluate the clinical feasibility of 68Ga-nitroimidazole-FAPI (NI-FAPI), targeting both hypoxia and fibroblast activation protein (FAP), in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: Thirty-two patients with gastrointestinal tumors (21 for initial staging, 11 for restaging) underwent both 68Ga-NI-FAPI and 18F-FDG PET/CT within 1 week. Immunohistochemistry for FAP and hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) was performed. Semiquantitative parameters including SUVmax, TBR, MTV, and total lesion FAP expression/glycolysis (TLF/TLG) were compared. Correlations between SUVmax and primary tumor depth, the short diameter of involved lymph nodes, and liver metastases were analyzed.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Immunohistochemistry confirmed FAP expression on cancer-associated fibroblasts and HIF-1α in tumor cytoplasm. 68Ga-NI-FAPI upgraded initial staging in 2 patients (9.52%). Among recurrent patients, its true positive rate was 100% versus 70% for 18F-FDG. 68Ga-NI-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated higher SUVmax and TBR in primary tumors (14.06±6.26 vs. 10.04±6.53, P=0.005; 12.30±6.80 vs. 6.52±4.38, P<0.001), particularly in signet-ring cell carcinoma (SRCC). It detected more metastases than 18F-FDG (306 vs. 263, P=0.003), with higher SUVmax and TBR in involved lymph nodes, liver metastases, peritoneal metastases, and other distant metastases (all P<0.05). SUVmax of 68Ga-NI-FAPI positively correlated with primary tumor depth (r=0.528, P=0.003), the short diameter of involved lymph nodes (r=0.304, P=0.032), and liver metastases (r=0.349, P=0.040).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: 68Ga-NI-FAPI exhibits superior diagnostic performance in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG, particularly in staging, SRCC evaluation, and metastasis detection. The positive correlation between tumor size and uptake supports its potential for patient selection in ligand-directed radionuclide therapy, establishing it as an effective theranostic agent for gastrointestinal tumors.

items.title: Primary Brain Sarcoma Presented on FDG PET/CT.
items.authors: Zheng K, Liu J, Zhu W, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion

sections.text: A 62-year-old man had dizziness and dysarthria for 4 months and limited mobility of the left upper extremity for 1 month. An outside enhanced MR showed a space-occupying lesion in the right frontal lobe. Since the patient had pancreaticoduodenectomy, gastrostomy, and jejunostomy 8.5 years ago for poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the small intestine, brain metastasis was suspected. FDG PET/CT demonstrated increased FDG activity in the right frontal lobe lesion, but no FDG-avid lesion was found in other parts of the body. Following surgical resection, histopathology examination indicated sarcoma. The patient underwent brain radiotherapy afterward.

items.title: A Case of Myoepithelioma Mimicking Metastasis on PSMA PET/CT: A Rare Pitfall Evaluated with MRI.
items.authors: Kibar A, Çelik AO, Yıldırım S, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: The patient underwent surgical excision, and the diagnosis of myoepithelioma was confirmed. This case highlights that myoepithelioma may represent a rare pitfall in PSMA PET/CT interpretation.

sections.text: Myoepithelioma is a rare neoplasm that is usually benign and is most often described in adults. We describe an incidental focus of increased PSMA uptake in the region of the distal phalanx of the great toe in a patient undergoing PSMA PET/CT for initial staging of prostate cancer. While the intense tracer accumulation was initially suspicious for an atypical solitary metastasis, subsequent MRI revealed a well-circumscribed soft tissue lesion. The patient underwent surgical excision, and the diagnosis of myoepithelioma was confirmed. This case highlights that myoepithelioma may represent a rare pitfall in PSMA PET/CT interpretation.

items.title: Scleroderma in Disguise: Symmetric Girdle-Muscle Uptake on 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT Revealing Inflammatory Myositis.
items.authors: Bailly M, Mazet R, Nicolas S, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Elevated creatine kinase, a late scleroderma-pattern capillaroscopy, and muscle MRI confirmed scleroderma-associated myositis. This case emphasizes that symmetric muscular prostate-specific membrane antigen uptake can reveal active inflammatory myositis.

sections.text: Prostate-specific membrane antigen-targeted PET agents are mainly used for prostate cancer; however, uptake in non-prostatic inflammatory tissue can challenge the physician. We report the case of a 75-year-old man referred for characterization of an FDG-avid prostate focus with normal PSA. 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT was performed. Incidental moderate symmetric uptake was found in the pelvic-girdle and paravertebral muscles, without morphologic correlate on CT. Elevated creatine kinase, a late scleroderma-pattern capillaroscopy, and muscle MRI confirmed scleroderma-associated myositis. This case emphasizes that symmetric muscular prostate-specific membrane antigen uptake can reveal active inflammatory myositis.
