sections.text: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) or scleroderma is a multisystem autoimmune disorder characterized by a variable pattern of skin thickening and involvement of visceral organs. The pathophysiology is similar across all organs, which is chronic low-grade inflammation, with vasculopathy and eventual fibrosis. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, particularly in patients with established disease comprising characteristic skin and visceral manifestations, with a supportive role of laboratory and imaging findings. The presence of radiologic signs such as hidebound bowel or a combination of patulous lower esophageal sphincter, pulmonary fibrosis, skin thickening, and Raynaud phenomenon is relatively specific for SSc. Nevertheless, imaging in SSc is primarily used to determine the pattern, severity, and complications of visceral organ involvement, rather than for diagnosis of SSc. Radiologic evaluation in SSc employs a wide gamut of investigations, depending on the organ of interest. For example, US is used for the skin and superficial tissues; fluoroscopy, CT, or MR enterography for the gastrointestinal tract; endoanal US or MRI for the internal anal sphincter; high-resolution CT for the lungs; echocardiography and cardiac MRI for SSc-related pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and cardiac disease; and radiography, CT, or MRI for musculoskeletal involvement. Early diagnosis of treatable features, such as PAH and gastroesophageal reflux, can help reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with SSc. Imaging is additionally useful to prognosticate and monitor the disease. The authors focus on the multisystem, multimodality imaging manifestations of SSc with relevant differential diagnoses to bridge the gaps in knowledge about SSc.

sections.text: Primary amenorrhea is the absence of menarche in a 15-year-old adolescent girl who has developed secondary sex characteristics or a 13-year-old girl without development. Primary amenorrhea reflects disruption along the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian-uterine axis and may arise from a spectrum of anatomic, genetic, or functional abnormalities. Although primary amenorrhea is less common than secondary amenorrhea, recognition of the underlying level of dysfunction is essential for appropriate diagnosis and management as well as informed counseling regarding the patient's reproductive potential. A structured anatomic approach allows categorization of the causes into three levels based on the predominant site of dysfunction: level I, which involves the uterus and vaginal outflow tract; level II, which involves the ovaries and gonads; and level III, which involves the hypothalamus and pituitary gland. This classification system emphasizes a systematic and multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and treatment, integrating clinical and biochemical testing and targeted imaging to localize the underlying dysfunction and guide treatment. Transabdominal US serves as the first-line imaging modality to help determine the presence and morphology of the pelvic organs. MRI provides detailed characterization of müllerian and urinary tract anomalies and allows evaluation of the hypothalamic-pituitary region when central causes are suspected.

sections.text: An 11-year-old girl with neuroblastoma, enrolled in a clinical trial, underwent 18F-MFBG PET/CT for treatment response evaluation. Imaging showed multiple metastatic lesions. This case demonstrates that physiological uterine 18F-MFBG uptake can occur during menstruation-a benign phenomenon that must be recognized to avoid false-positive interpretation of PET/CT findings.

sections.text: Isolated bilateral renal metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is extremely rare. We report a 63-year-old man with ESCC treated with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and esophagectomy followed by anti-PD-1 maintenance, in whom follow-up 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated multiple bilateral renal lesions with intense 18F-FDG uptake. CT-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. This case highlights that new isolated renal lesions during cancer immunotherapy should not be assumed to be immune-related nephritis and underscores the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT and biopsy in establishing the diagnosis.

sections.text: Prostate cancer metastasis to the spermatic cord is exceedingly rare. A 64-year-old man with a history of robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy for high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma (pT3b, Gleason 3+5=9) originating from a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left prostate hemisphere presented with biochemical recurrence (PSA: 3.77 ng/mL) 6 years postoperatively. Whole-body 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT revealed a solitary, hypermetabolic nodular mass in the contralateral (right) spermatic cord (SUVmax: 23.0), without local or distant metastasis. Surgical excision confirmed metastatic prostatic adenocarcinoma. This case highlights the crucial role of 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT in detecting atypical soft tissue oligometastases and underscores a potential contralateral dissemination mechanism via pelvic vascular collaterals.

items.title: Peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics for predicting early progression of hepatocellular carcinoma after microwave ablation: development and external validation of a clinical-radiomics model.
items.authors: Fu Y, Jiao L, Yu P, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Peri-ablational AP + PP CT radiomics combined with AFP and tumor size demonstrated good discrimination for early HCC progression after MWA and may facilitate individualized risk assessment, pending further validation.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To develop and externally validate a peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics model for predicting early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression after microwave ablation (MWA) and to assess its incremental value over clinical predictors.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective multicenter study included 376 patients in training (n = 235), internal validation (n = 60), and external validation (n = 81) cohorts. Early progression was defined as local tumor progression or new intrahepatic HCC within 1 year after MWA. Radiomics features were extracted from 5-mm peri-ablational regions on multiphasic CT obtained 1-2 months after MWA. Six machine-learning algorithms and phase combinations were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was combined with independent clinical predictors. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and model interpretability were assessed.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The arterial-plus-portal venous phase (AP + PP) multilayer perceptron model achieved AUCs of 0.857, 0.815, and 0.903 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively, with performance comparable to the three-phase model. Log10 AFP and tumor size > 2 cm were independent clinical predictors. The combined clinical-radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.884, and 0.963, respectively. In external validation, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 84.2%, 96.8%, and 93.8%, respectively. SHAP analysis identified the radiomics score as the most influential predictor.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Peri-ablational AP + PP CT radiomics combined with AFP and tumor size demonstrated good discrimination for early HCC progression after MWA and may facilitate individualized risk assessment, pending further validation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence methods for HER2 status assessment: a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis.
items.authors: V S, Das CJ

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an important predictive and prognostic biomarker that guides targeted therapy, particularly in breast and gastric cancers. Conventional HER2 assessment using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is limited by inter-observer variability, heterogeneous expression, and diagnostic complexity.

sections.text: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an important predictive and prognostic biomarker that guides targeted therapy, particularly in breast and gastric cancers. Conventional HER2 assessment using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is limited by inter-observer variability, heterogeneous expression, and diagnostic complexity. This systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to evaluate Artificial Intelligence-based HER2 assessment. Fifty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and 14 in the diagnostic meta-analysis. Bibliometric analysis, methodological taxonomy, comparative evaluation, and pooled diagnostic performance were assessed, with study quality evaluated using QUADAS-2. AI methodologies have rapidly evolved from conventional machine learning and radiomics to deep learning, Vision Transformers, explainable AI, and multimodal frameworks, with histopathology and Magnetic Resonance Imaging. being the most frequently used modalities. Research activity increased markedly between 2023 and 2025. Pooled sensitivity was 87.8%, specificity was 83.5%, and Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (SROC AUC) was 0.852 (95% CI: 0.801-0.881), indicating promising overall diagnostic performance. Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test showed no significant evidence of publication bias (p = 0.14). However, heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Heterogeneous datasets, limited external validation, and inconsistent evaluation methods remain important barriers to clinical implementation. Future research should emphasize multicenter prospective validation, explainable and multimodal AI, foundation models, federated learning, and evaluation in underexplored malignancies, including gallbladder cancer.

items.title: Fat saturation on T2-weighted imaging in the assessment of renal masses and its impact on clear cell likelihood score categorization.
items.authors: Caglic I, Kolumam Parameswaran P, Xi Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Fat saturation introduces a systematic upward bias in qualitative T2 signal assessment of small renal masses. Although ccLS reclassification was less frequent and overall agreement remained high, this bias may alter ccLS assignment, particularly in lesions with inherently low T2 signal intensity, supporting standardized NFS-T2W acquisition when applying the ccLS.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To evaluate the impact of fat saturation on T2-weighted (T2W) imaging in the assessment of small renal masses (SRMs; cT1a ≤ 4 cm) with the clear cell likelihood score (ccLS).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective study included 147 histologically confirmed SRMs evaluated with MRI including non-fat saturated (NFS) and fat saturated (FS) T2W fast spin echo acquisitions. Two readers (R1, R2) assigned qualitative T2 signal categories (hypo-, iso-, hyperintense), with sequence-specific ccLS scores recalculated while all non-T2 ccLS components were held constant. Agreement, sequence-related reclassification, and inter-reader agreement were assessed for T2 signal intensity and ccLS scores. Cumulative link mixed models (CLMMs) were used to assess sequence-related shifts in ordinal category. Quantitative mass-to-cortex signal-intensity ratios were compared between sequences using Bland-Altman analysis.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Qualitative agreement between sequences was 74% and 65% for R1 and R2, respectively. FS-T2W was associated with over four-fold greater cumulative odds of a higher qualitative T2 signal category than NFS-T2W (OR, 4.68; 95% CI, 2.91-7.52; p < 0.001), with upgrading in 20% (R1) and 30% (R2) of lesions versus downgrading in 5% for both readers. Qualitative inter-reader agreement was substantial (κ = 0.77 for NFS-T2W; κ = 0.73 for FS-T2W). Mass-to-cortex ratios were higher on FS-T2W (median 1.30 vs. 1.15; p < 0.001), corresponding to a mean proportional increase of 17.9% (95% CI, 12.4-23.4%). ccLS concordance remained high between NFS-T2W and FS-T2W (R1: 94% and R2: 90%; weighted κ = 0.944 and 0.918). FS-T2W was associated with greater cumulative odds of a higher ccLS category than NFS-T2W (OR, 4.27; 95% CI, 1.52-12.0; p = 0.006). Inter-reader agreement for ccLS was almost perfect (weighted κ = 0.98 for NFS-T2W; 0.95 for FS-T2W).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Fat saturation introduces a systematic upward bias in qualitative T2 signal assessment of small renal masses. Although ccLS reclassification was less frequent and overall agreement remained high, this bias may alter ccLS assignment, particularly in lesions with inherently low T2 signal intensity, supporting standardized NFS-T2W acquisition when applying the ccLS.

items.title: CT-based machine learning and multimodal prediction in acute pancreatitis: a narrative review.
items.authors: Li T, Zhang B, Mai G

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Acute pancreatitis (AP) has a highly variable clinical course. This narrative review focuses on computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep learning and clinical-imaging models for severity and adverse-outcome prediction, with clinical-only models as context.

sections.text: Acute pancreatitis (AP) has a highly variable clinical course. This narrative review focuses on computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep learning and clinical-imaging models for severity and adverse-outcome prediction, with clinical-only models as context. A targeted PubMed search checked on 16 October 2026, with a publication cutoff of 14 October 2026, retrieved 80 unique records; ten CT-informed exemplars and eight clinical-context studies were selected for detailed comparison. This is a representative, non-exhaustive synthesis. For severe AP (SAP) prediction, reported same-center internal or temporal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.852 to 0.894, and reported external-test AUCs from 0.887 to 0.916; one validation cohort of unconfirmed independence had an AUC of 0.920. These descriptive ranges do not establish model superiority or characterize all retrieved studies. CT protocols and input timing, endpoint definitions, sampling and validation designs varied. Predominantly retrospective evidence, uncertain prediction landmarks, incomplete calibration and threshold reporting, and limited prospective impact assessment constrain translation. Feature explanations describe model associations rather than causal intervention targets. Imaging artificial intelligence (AI) remains an adjunct to clinical assessment; independent validation, calibration, decision-curve appraisal and prospective workflow/outcome evaluation are needed before clinical-pathway integration.

items.title: (Elastography) E-BI-RADS: A Novel Classification System for Breast Elastography to Enable Safe Biopsy De-escalation.
items.authors: Barr RG, Pfob A, Bauman P, et al.

conclusion.label: Discussion
conclusion.text: E-BI-RADS provides the first standardized, BI-RADS-like classification system for breast elastography and enables safe biopsy de-escalation with excellent sensitivity and improved specificity compared with existing approaches.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: Determining the probability of malignancy of a breast lesion allows for the appropriate triage of follow-up. Although BI-RADS provides standardized risk stratification for mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, no equivalent classification system exists for breast elastography. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a data-driven E-BI-RADS classification for breast elastography and to compare its diagnostic performance with B-mode BI-RADS.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: In this retrospective study, consecutive patients undergoing breast imaging with available B-mode ultrasound, shear-wave elastography (SWE), and strain elastography (10L4 transducer, Siemens ACUSON Sequoia) from 06/2023 to 12/2025 were included. A multivariable logistic regression model combining SWE velocity and elastography-to-B-mode lesion size (E/B) ratio was used to estimate malignancy probability, followed by Platt recalibration. Data-driven probability cutoffs were derived to define E-BI-RADS categories aligned with the BI-RADS concept. (E-)BI-RADS categories 4 and 5 were considered an indication for biopsy. Histopathologic evaluation or imaging follow-up served as the reference standard.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The cohort comprised 344 breast lesions in 337 patients, including 224 (65.1%) malignant and 120 (34.9%) benign lesions. B-mode BI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 98.6% (221/224) and a specificity of 34.2% (41/120). E-BI-RADS demonstrated malignancy rates of 0.0% in E-BI-RADS 2 (0/71); 5.3% in E-BI-RADS 3 (1/19); 85.2% in E-BI-RADS 4 (155/182); and 94.4% in E-BI-RADS 5 (68/70). E-BI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 99.6% (223/224) and a specificity of 74.2% (89/120). The single false-negative case was a 31 mm B-cell lymphoma, classified as E-BI-RADS 3, with a shear-wave velocity of 4.4 m/s and an E/B ratio of 0.9. Decision-curve analysis demonstrates that E-BI-RADS achieves higher net benefit than SWE-based and B-mode BI-RADS strategies.

sections.label: Discussion
sections.text: E-BI-RADS provides the first standardized, BI-RADS-like classification system for breast elastography and enables safe biopsy de-escalation with excellent sensitivity and improved specificity compared with existing approaches.

items.title: Commercially available AI medical devices for prostate MRI: current evidence and opportunities for implementation.
items.authors: Pakpoor J, Bhanji Y, van Leeuwen KG, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Evidence supporting the use of commercial AI for prostate MRI remains limited and heterogeneous, with inconsistent diagnostic benefits. Prospective comparative studies in real clinical workflows are needed to determine its potential role within the prostate cancer diagnostic pathway.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Evidence for clinical implementation of prostate AI remains limited-most studies are retrospective and single-centre, with heterogeneous populations and reference standards. Findings AI may improve diagnostic performance for less-experienced readers, but gains for expert readers and assessment of workflow efficiency are limited. Clinical relevance Prospective multicentre studies embedded in real-world pathways are needed, together with analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes.

sections.label: Objective
sections.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve prostate MRI interpretation and reduce radiologist workload, but evidence supporting clinical implementation remains limited. This scoping review summarises evidence on commercially available AI medical devices for prostate MRI.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: PubMed was searched for studies published through October 1, 2026. Eligible devices were cleared by the United States Food and Drug Administration and/or CE marked, with commercial availability corroborated through manufacturer websites. Data extraction addressed standalone AI performance, AI-assisted radiologist performance, workflow efficiency, and downstream clinical impact.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Twenty-one studies evaluating 7 commercial AI systems were included; 17/21 (81%) were retrospective and 14/21 (67%) were single-centre. AI assistance suggested greater benefit for less-experienced readers, but improvements were inconsistent and increased specificity sometimes accompanied reduced sensitivity. Standalone evaluations, outside the devices' approved intended use, showed discrimination comparable to that of radiologists in selected cohorts. Inter-reader agreement and workflow benefits were mixed. We identify three key limitations of the current body of evidence that require thoughtful consideration before routine implementation: (1) incomplete verification strategies, (2) limited determination of workflow benefit, and (3) lack of analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes, e.g., time to treat or cancer-free survival.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Evidence supporting the use of commercial AI for prostate MRI remains limited and heterogeneous, with inconsistent diagnostic benefits. Prospective comparative studies in real clinical workflows are needed to determine its potential role within the prostate cancer diagnostic pathway.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: Question Evidence for clinical implementation of prostate AI remains limited-most studies are retrospective and single-centre, with heterogeneous populations and reference standards. Findings AI may improve diagnostic performance for less-experienced readers, but gains for expert readers and assessment of workflow efficiency are limited. Clinical relevance Prospective multicentre studies embedded in real-world pathways are needed, together with analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes.

items.title: Comprehensive multi-organ and body composition phenotyping identifies metabolic signatures associated with incident type 2 diabetes.
items.authors: Kim S, Kim DW, Kim S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Whole-body MRI-derived multi-organ biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM and enhanced risk stratification beyond an established clinical risk score. Muscle fat fraction may better reflect metabolic risk than muscle volume in IMAT-rich regions.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Clinical risk scores miss the multi-organ pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes; does whole-body MRI organ size and fat quantification improve prediction of incident diabetes? Findings Eight MRI-derived biomarkers independently predicted incident type 2 diabetes; a deep learning model using whole-body MRI biomarkers reached a concordance index of 0.814. Clinical relevance Automated whole-body MRI biomarkers capture multi-organ metabolic signatures beyond conventional risk scoring. Applied after clinical screening, they remove 43.0% of false-positive classifications while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To derive a multi-organ imaging biomarker panel from whole-body MRI and evaluate its predictive value for incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including the role of intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) in reconciling discrepancies between muscle volume and metabolic risk.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 46,129 UK Biobank participants without diabetes at the time of imaging. Organ volume indices and fat fractions were extracted from Dixon MRI through automated segmentation. Associations between muscle volume indices, fat fractions, and handgrip strength were evaluated, and IMAT was graded in strength-matched participants. Independent imaging biomarkers were identified using adjusted Cox models, and a deep learning model was trained. Added value relative to the Leicester risk assessment score was evaluated using decision curve analysis.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: During follow-up, 600 participants developed T2DM. Eight biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM, including liver volume index (hazard ratio (HR), 1.28; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.19-1.38), pancreas fat fraction (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.10-1.28), and gluteus fat fraction (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.08-1.27). Gluteal IMAT grades were higher in weak-for-volume participants than in strength-matched controls (median, 2.0 vs 1.0; p = 0.02). The deep learning model achieved a concordance index of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.797-0.832) and, when applied sequentially with clinical criteria, reduced false-positive classifications by 43.0% while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Whole-body MRI-derived multi-organ biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM and enhanced risk stratification beyond an established clinical risk score. Muscle fat fraction may better reflect metabolic risk than muscle volume in IMAT-rich regions.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: Question Clinical risk scores miss the multi-organ pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes; does whole-body MRI organ size and fat quantification improve prediction of incident diabetes? Findings Eight MRI-derived biomarkers independently predicted incident type 2 diabetes; a deep learning model using whole-body MRI biomarkers reached a concordance index of 0.814. Clinical relevance Automated whole-body MRI biomarkers capture multi-organ metabolic signatures beyond conventional risk scoring. Applied after clinical screening, they remove 43.0% of false-positive classifications while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

items.title: Preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma using multi-sequence MRI radiomics: a non-contrast approach integrating T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and apparent diffusion coefficient imaging.
items.authors: Zhang Y, Bao Y, Huang G, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: In this single-center, internally validated study, non-contrast multi-sequence MRI radiomics models integrating T2WI, DWI, and ADC showed moderate discrimination of Ki-67 expression in HCC. The contrast-free strategy is potentially applicable to patients with contraindications to gadolinium and warrants external validation; These findings represent internal validation only and require confirmation in external, preferably prospective multicenter, cohorts before any clinical application can be considered.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Ki-67 is a key immunohistochemical marker of tumor proliferative activity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, non-invasive assessment of Ki-67 status before surgery remains an unmet clinical need. This study aimed to develop and internally validate multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics models based exclusively on non-contrast sequences for preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective study included 91 patients with 97 pathologically confirmed HCC lesions ( high Ki-67, ≥ 10%, n = 55; low Ki-67, < 10%, n = 42). Three-dimensional volumes of interest were manually segmented on T2-weighted imaging ( T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging ( DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient ( ADC) maps, and 5055 radiomic features ( approximately 1684 per sequence) were extracted were extracted from the three sequences. After feature selection with Pearson correlation coefficient filtering and the Kruskal-Wallis test, three multilayer perceptron ( MLP) models were constructed: Model-T ( T2WI), Model-D ( DWI + ADC), and Model-M ( combined T2WI, DWI, and ADC). The models were developed with five-fold cross-validation in the training cohort and were evaluated in a held-out testing cohort. This was a single-center retrospective study, and validation was internal only. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ( AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: No significant differences in clinical characteristics were observed between the high and low Ki-67 groups. In the training cohort, the apparent (resubstitution) AUCs of Model-T, Model-D, and Model-M were 0.715, 0.823, and 0.860, respectively (representing model fit rather than cross-validated performance). In the held-out testing cohort, the corresponding AUCs were 0.707, 0.692, and 0.716. In the testing cohort, Model-M achieved a sensitivity of 68.8%, a specificity of 53.8%, and an accuracy of 62.1%, whereas Model-D showed the most balanced performance (sensitivity, 68.8%; specificity, 76.9%; accuracy, 72.4%). The dominant features were texture features derived predominantly from the ADC sequence. The cross-validated training AUCs were considerably lower (range, 0.522-0.585).

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: In this single-center, internally validated study, non-contrast multi-sequence MRI radiomics models integrating T2WI, DWI, and ADC showed moderate discrimination of Ki-67 expression in HCC. The contrast-free strategy is potentially applicable to patients with contraindications to gadolinium and warrants external validation; These findings represent internal validation only and require confirmation in external, preferably prospective multicenter, cohorts before any clinical application can be considered.

items.title: T1 mapping-based heterogeneity analysis of Gd-EOB-DTPA-enhanced MRI in cirrhotic nodules: biological basis, emerging evidence, and future perspectives.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Liver cirrhosis is a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and accurate risk stratification of cirrhotic nodules remains a clinical challenge. During hepatocarcinogenesis, regenerative and dysplastic nodules undergo heterogeneous alterations in hepatocyte function, transporter expression, vascular architecture, and tissue composition.

sections.text: Liver cirrhosis is a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and accurate risk stratification of cirrhotic nodules remains a clinical challenge. During hepatocarcinogenesis, regenerative and dysplastic nodules undergo heterogeneous alterations in hepatocyte function, transporter expression, vascular architecture, and tissue composition. However, conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment of intranodular signal heterogeneity largely relies on subjective visual interpretation and lacks standardized and reproducible quantitative biomarkers. Gadoxetic acid disodium (Gd-EOB-DTPA)-enhanced MRI provides functional information during the hepatobiliary phase by reflecting hepatocyte-specific uptake mediated by organic anion transporting polypeptides. Impaired transporter expression during malignant transformation is associated with reduced contrast uptake and may contribute to spatially heterogeneous contrast distribution. Quantitative T1 mapping enables voxel-wise measurement of absolute T1 relaxation times, thereby providing an objective and quantitative approach to tissue characterization. However, most existing studies have primarily focused on mean T1 values or global reduction rates, while intranodular spatial heterogeneity remains insufficiently explored. MRI-based heterogeneity analysis may complement conventional mean-value analysis by capturing regional variations within lesions. However, direct evidence on T1 mapping-derived heterogeneity in cirrhotic nodules remains limited, and its incremental value over mean T1 values for reflecting hepatocellular function or early malignant transformation has not been established. Quantitative heterogeneity descriptors, including standard deviation, coefficient of variation, histogram-based parameters, and texture features, can objectively characterize the magnitude and distribution of spatial T1 variation and provide a quantitative framework for assessing intralesional heterogeneity. This review summarizes the biological rationale, technical principles, and emerging evidence regarding Gd-EOB-DTPA-enhanced T1 mapping for the assessment of intranodular heterogeneity. It further discusses its potential role in malignant transformation risk stratification of cirrhotic nodules, current limitations, and future directions for clinical translation.

items.title: Impact of reader expertise on PI-RADS assessment of prostate transition zone lesions: Diagnostic performance, inter-reader agreement, and resource implications.
items.authors: Spoto F, Demozzi E, Monterubbiano L, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Specialized interpretation was associated with higher diagnostic yield for TZ lesions, particularly PI-RADS 4. Reader-dependent application of the erased-margins criterion is a candidate mechanism requiring confirmation and a potential training target rather than a stand-alone rule; prospective external validation is needed.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: PI-RADS scoring of transition zone (TZ) lesions is strongly reader-dependent, particularly in the PI-RADS 4 category. We compared diagnostic performance and inter-reader agreement between a specialized high-volume center and non-specialized referring centers.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: Overall, 315 men with a TZ lesion scored PI-RADS ≥ 3 underwent MRI-guided in-bore biopsy and were stratified by interpreting site (non-specialized vs specialized). The erased-margins criterion was reassessed centrally by one specialized-center reader (the biopsy operator) and, in a 125-lesion subset, by three independent readers.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Positive predictive value for clinically significant cancer (csPCa, Grade Group ≥ 2) at PI-RADS ≥ 4 was higher in the specialized cohort (43.3% vs 29.5%, p = 0.015). For PI-RADS 4 lesions, detection of any cancer was 76.9% vs 42.6% (p < 0.001), but not significantly different for csPCa (32.1% vs 22.8%, p = 0.16). On central reassessment, non-specialized centers had more often assigned PI-RADS 4 to lesions without erased margins (50% vs 35%, p = 0.048), a difference not replicated by the three independent readers. Agreement on PI-RADS category was substantial within and moderate between centers (κ 0.68 vs 0.43-0.49); agreement on the erased-margins criterion was fair-to-moderate (Fleiss κ 0.30), and its discriminative value decreased with decreasing expertise (AUC 0.82, 0.75, 0.70), largely reflecting lesion identification. The central reassessment did not outperform blinded readers (AUC 0.69).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Specialized interpretation was associated with higher diagnostic yield for TZ lesions, particularly PI-RADS 4. Reader-dependent application of the erased-margins criterion is a candidate mechanism requiring confirmation and a potential training target rather than a stand-alone rule; prospective external validation is needed.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Compared with the T2WI model and VI-RADS assessment, the Joint model demonstrated better diagnostic performance and generalizability for predicting muscle invasion in patients with bladder cancer.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Reliable noninvasive tools for preoperative prediction of muscle invasion in bladder cancer are lacking, as TURBT-based staging carries procedural risks and frequent understaging. Findings A biparametric MRI deep learning model achieved AUCs of 0.907-0.979 across internal and external validation cohorts, outperforming T2WI-only models and VI-RADS. Critical relevance statement Contrast-free biparametric MRI combined with deep learning enables accurate, generalizable preoperative prediction of muscle invasion, offering particular value for equivocal VI-RADS 2-3 lesions and supporting noninvasive clinical decision-making.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning model that integrates T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for the noninvasive prediction of muscle invasion in bladder cancer.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: A total of 308 bladder tumors from 254 patients were retrospectively collected from three institutions. Of these, 177 tumors from Center 1 were partitioned via stratified sampling into a training set (n = 128) and an internal validation set (n = 49). The remaining two centers contributed 59 and 72 tumors, respectively, which served as external validation cohorts. A dual-branch 3D deep convolutional neural network (Joint model) based on biparametric MRI (bp-MRI) was developed using the training data and compared with a deep learning model based on T2WI (T2WI model) and VI-RADS assessments by radiologists. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The Joint model achieved mean AUCs of 0.979 ± 0.007 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.907 ± 0.013 and 0.916 ± 0.021 in the external validation cohorts. It outperformed the T2WI model in all cohorts and achieved higher AUCs than radiologists across all validation cohorts. Notably, for equivocal VI-RADS 2-3 lesions, the Joint model yielded higher accuracy than the T2WI model in external validation.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Compared with the T2WI model and VI-RADS assessment, the Joint model demonstrated better diagnostic performance and generalizability for predicting muscle invasion in patients with bladder cancer.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and stage 2-3 fibrosis: a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled study.
items.authors: Lawitz E, Wong VW, Shankar RR, et al.

conclusion.label: Interpretation
conclusion.text: Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: We did a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study conducted at 176 academic and community centres in 26 countries. We included adults (aged ≥18 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage 2 or stage 3 fibrosis. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) to receive either efinopegdutide (4 mg, 7 mg, or 10 mg), placebo, or open-label semaglutide 2·4 mg, all administered subcutaneously once weekly. Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete.

sections.label: Findings
sections.text: Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. We randomly assigned 386 (23%) participants, of whom 381 (99%; 194 [51%] women and 187 [49%] men) received at least one dose of study intervention and were included in the analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). At week 52, MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis occurred in 31 (56%) of 55 participants in the 4 mg efinopegdutide group, 31 (63%) of 49 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 35 (61%) of 57 participants in the 10 mg efinopegdutide group versus seven (13%) of 53 participants in the placebo group (difference vs placebo 43·0 percentage points [95% CI 25·7 to 57·8; p<0·0001] for 4 mg, 49·5 percentage points [31·4 to 64·2; p<0·0001] for 7 mg, and 47·8 percentage points [30·7 to 62·0; p<0·0001] for 10 mg); 26 (53%) of 49 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. For the key secondary endpoint, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis occurred in 32 (43%) of 75 participants in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 39 (52%) of 75 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 26 (34%) of 77 participants in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group versus 16 (21%) of 77 participants receiving placebo (difference vs placebo 21·7 percentage points [7·1 to 35·7; p=0·0038] in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 30·4 percentage points [15·4 to 44·3; p<0·0001] in the efinopegdutide 7 mg group, and 13·0 percentage points [-1·2 to 26·8; p=0·072] in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group); 16 (25%) of 65 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. The most frequently reported adverse events with efinopegdutide were gastrointestinal, with the highest rates among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg. Adverse events leading to discontinuation of study intervention occurred more frequently among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg (nine [11%] of 79 participants) compared with the other doses of efinopegdutide (range 3-4%) or placebo (one [1%]).

sections.label: Interpretation
sections.text: Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH.

items.title: A "Hot" Sulfur Colloid Clue in a Hypervascular Pediatric Liver Mass: Resolving a Large Focal Nodular Hyperplasia Mimicking Fibrolamellar Hepatocellular Carcinoma.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion

sections.text: Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) in young children may mimic malignancy when large and markedly hypervascular. A 5-year-old girl with no known predisposing factors presented with painless abdominal distension and hepatomegaly. Serum alpha-fetoprotein and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin were normal. MRI showed a hypervascular hepatic mass with stellate central scar, abnormal intralesional vessels, and intrahepatic arteriovenous shunting, concerning for fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (FLHCC). Subsequent ⁹⁹ᵐTc-sulfur-colloid scintigraphy demonstrated near-homogeneous tracer uptake within the lesion, mildly lower than the normal liver. The preserved Kupffer-cell function favored FNH, likely arising as a hyperplastic response to altered local perfusion. Clinical surveillance supported the benign diagnosis.

items.title: Reverse PSMA Theranostic Discordance: Reproducible ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 Uptake in Skeletal Metastases Inconspicuous on Serial ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT.
items.authors: Mahdi RA, Sood A, Sharma S, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: This case of "reverse theranostic discordance" challenges the assumption that diagnostic PSMA PET faithfully represents the full target landscape for radioligand therapy. Systematic SPECT/CT review after treatment cycles may reveal therapeutically relevant disease invisible to pretherapy PET.

sections.text: 18F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT is widely used for selecting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) for 177Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy. We present a striking case in which multiple skeletal metastases demonstrated intense, reproducible ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 uptake on post-therapy scintigraphy across all three treatment cycles, yet remained occult or only minimally avid on serial ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT. SPECT/CT confirmed anatomic lesion localization, excluding artifact. This case of "reverse theranostic discordance" challenges the assumption that diagnostic PSMA PET faithfully represents the full target landscape for radioligand therapy. Systematic SPECT/CT review after treatment cycles may reveal therapeutically relevant disease invisible to pretherapy PET.

sections.text: A 54-year-old man with back pain showed lytic vertebral lesions on MRI. 18F-FDG PET/CT revealed an FDG-avid thyroid primary, skeletal metastases, and a relatively low FDG-avid right renal lesion. Thyroid histopathology confirmed follicular carcinoma. Post-thyroidectomy radioiodine scan demonstrated intense uptake in both skeletal and renal lesions. Biopsy from the renal lesion confirmed renal metastasis. Renal involvement in differentiated thyroid cancer is rare and may demonstrate concordant FDG and radioiodine avidity.

items.title: 68Ga‑PSMA PET/CT Facilitates Identification of a Rare Rectal Metastasis From Prostate Cancer.
items.authors: Zhang Z, Yang Y, Zuo C, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Final pathology confirmed metastatic prostate cancer to the rectum. For patients with a history of prostate cancer presenting with rectal occupying lesions, metastatic disease should be included in the differential diagnosis.

sections.text: An 86-year-old man underwent radical prostatectomy for prostate adenocarcinoma (T3aN0M0) 5 years ago. He presented with recurrent constipation for 5 months. Pelvic MRI raised suspicion of rectal cancer. Serum prostate specific antigen (PSA) was mildly elevated (9.610 ng/mL). PET/CT revealed thickened rectal walls with no significant hypermetabolism on 18F‑FDG imaging, but marked radiotracer uptake on 68Ga‑PSMA imaging (SUVmax = 22.4). Final pathology confirmed metastatic prostate cancer to the rectum. For patients with a history of prostate cancer presenting with rectal occupying lesions, metastatic disease should be included in the differential diagnosis.

items.title: 18F-FAPI PET/CT and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance for Cardiac Fibrotic Process in End-stage Renal Disease: A Pilot Study.
items.authors: Wu T, Luo C, Yang G, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: 18F-FAPI PET enables in vivo detection of cardiac fibroblast activation in ESRD and correlates with functional and tissue parameters by CMR. FAPI uptake may serve as an imaging biomarker for cardiac remodeling. Further studies are warranted to clarify the role of 18F-FAPI PET in evaluating the efficacy of anti-fibrotic treatment and in assisting cardiac risk stratification in ESRD patients.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) increases the risk of myocardial fibrosis. This study aimed to detect cardiac fibroblast activation and fibrosis in ESRD using 18F-labeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR).

sections.label: Patients and methods
sections.text: This prospective clinical trial (NCT07107919) enrolled 33 ESRD patients who underwent 18F-FAPI PET/CT, with 19 patients undergoing CMR. Myocardial FAPI activity was quantified. Cardiac function [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF), left atrial ejection fraction (LAEF)] and tissue parameters [native T1, extracellular volume (ECV), late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)] were assessed by CMR. Spearman correlation analysis assessed correlations between 18F-FAPI uptake and CMR parameters.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: A total of 75.76% (25/33) of ESRD patients showed myocardial FAPI uptake, significantly higher than the controls (P < 0.05). 18F-FAPI-42 PET identified more segments with evidence of fibroblast activation than CMR-late gadolinium enhancement detected fibrosis (82 vs. 71). Compared with FAPI-negative patients, FAPI-positive patients had increased native-T1, decreased LVEF, LAEF and RVEF (P < 0.05). FAPI-positive segments showed higher native-T1 and extracellular volume % than FAPI-negative segments (P < 0.05). FAPI activity correlated with LVEF, RVEF, LAEF and native-T1. Higher myocardial FAPI uptake was associated with lower LVEF and longer dialysis duration.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: 18F-FAPI PET enables in vivo detection of cardiac fibroblast activation in ESRD and correlates with functional and tissue parameters by CMR. FAPI uptake may serve as an imaging biomarker for cardiac remodeling. Further studies are warranted to clarify the role of 18F-FAPI PET in evaluating the efficacy of anti-fibrotic treatment and in assisting cardiac risk stratification in ESRD patients.

items.title: Dual-tracer 18F-FDG and 18F-PSMA PET/CT Findings in Metastatic Scrotal Extramammary Paget Disease Initially Suspected as Prostate Cancer.
items.authors: Bai L, Gu B, Liu W, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: PET/CT showed intense FDG and PSMA uptake in widespread osseous and nodal lesions, whereas the prostate showed no focal FDG uptake or abnormal PSMA uptake. This discordant imaging pattern, together with clinical and pathologic correlation, supported metastatic scrotal extramammary Paget disease rather than prostate cancer.

sections.text: We present dual-tracer 18F-FDG and 18F-PSMA (prostate-specific membrane antigen) PET/CT findings in a 75-year-old man with prior scrotal extramammary Paget disease who developed diffuse bone and lymph node lesions. L1 vertebral biopsy initially favored metastatic prostatic acinar adenocarcinoma, but serum prostate-specific antigen was 0.567 ng/mL and prostate biopsies were benign. PET/CT showed intense FDG and PSMA uptake in widespread osseous and nodal lesions, whereas the prostate showed no focal FDG uptake or abnormal PSMA uptake. This discordant imaging pattern, together with clinical and pathologic correlation, supported metastatic scrotal extramammary Paget disease rather than prostate cancer.

sections.text: A 66-year-old woman with left upper abdominal pain had a solitary splenic mass nearly inconspicuous on unenhanced CT but progressively enhancing, although hypoattenuating relative to adjacent splenic parenchyma, on contrast-enhanced CT. 18F-FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax, 15.1) without additional suspicious hypermetabolic foci within the imaged field of view. CT suggested a potentially malignant splenic neoplasm, with lymphoma among the preoperative considerations. Splenectomy confirmed Rosai-Dorfman disease. No recurrence was identified on CT at 10 months. This case illustrates the broad differential diagnosis of solitary FDG-avid splenic masses.

conclusion.text: This case demonstrates 18F-PSMA PET/CT detection at a low PSA level of a clinically occult metastatic lesion involving the cecum, an exceptionally rare site for prostate cancer spread. Colonoscopy and biopsy confirmation of atypical PSMA-avid gastrointestinal lesions remain essential, as physiologic colonic uptake, PSMA-avid diverticula, and PSMA-expressing primary colorectal cancers are well-documented mimickers.

sections.text: We present a patient with biochemical recurrence after salvage radiation and combined androgen deprivation therapy with abiraterone who underwent 18F-PSMA PET/CT for a rapidly rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA). The scan revealed an intense prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-avid focus in the cecum without an apparent CT correlate. Colonoscopy identified a smooth, 2 cm nonobstructing cecal mass, and biopsy confirmed metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma by morphology and immunohistochemistry. This case demonstrates 18F-PSMA PET/CT detection at a low PSA level of a clinically occult metastatic lesion involving the cecum, an exceptionally rare site for prostate cancer spread. Colonoscopy and biopsy confirmation of atypical PSMA-avid gastrointestinal lesions remain essential, as physiologic colonic uptake, PSMA-avid diverticula, and PSMA-expressing primary colorectal cancers are well-documented mimickers.
