items.title: [18F]DOPA PET Reveals Metabolically Active Transcriptomic States Associated with Clinical Outcome in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Imperiale A, Lu X, Fattori A, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Conclusion: [18F]DOPA PET uptake was associated with amino acid-driven metabolic programs in panNETs, including SLC7A5 expression, and adverse clinical features. These findings suggest that [18F]DOPA uptake may provide a noninvasive readout of tumor metabolic activity, although its value as an imaging biomarker requires independent validation.

sections.text: [18F]fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]DOPA) uptake is dependent on amino acid transport and decarboxylation pathways, including large neutral amino acid transporter 1, encoded by SLC7A5, which are linked to tumor aggressiveness. This study evaluated whether in vivo uptake of [18F]DOPA can serve as an imaging biomarker for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (panNETs), reflecting a tumor's transcriptional status and a patient's clinical course. Methods: This retrospective single-center study was based on a transcriptomic cohort of 74 primary panNETs. A subset of 22 panNETs from patients who underwent preoperative [18F]DOPA PET/CT constituted the discovery radiotranscriptomic cohort. [18F]DOPA tumor uptake was quantified using SUVmax and integrated with matched RNA-sequencing data. Unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment, and tumor microenvironment deconvolution were performed to identify transcriptional programs associated with [18F]DOPA uptake. The prognostic value of SLC7A5 was evaluated in the discovery cohort, the full transcriptomic cohort (n = 74), and an independent external cohort (n = 33). Results: Unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles identified 2 robust molecular subtypes: cluster 1 and cluster 2. Cluster 1 showed higher [18F]DOPA uptake than did cluster 2, with a median SUVmax of 24.3 versus 5.9, respectively (P = 0.030), and was associated with more advanced clinicopathologic features and shorter event-free survival. This subtype was also characterized by enrichment in extracellular matrix, stromal, vascular, and immune-related components, along with upregulation of amino acid transport and amine metabolism genes, including SLC7A5 As a mechanistic link between tracer uptake and tumor metabolism, SLC7A5 expression significantly stratified event-free survival in the discovery cohort and remained prognostic in the full cohort. Conclusion: [18F]DOPA PET uptake was associated with amino acid-driven metabolic programs in panNETs, including SLC7A5 expression, and adverse clinical features. These findings suggest that [18F]DOPA uptake may provide a noninvasive readout of tumor metabolic activity, although its value as an imaging biomarker requires independent validation.

items.title: Targeted α-Therapy with 211At-Labeled Trastuzumab Overcomes Trastuzumab Resistance in Uterine Serous Carcinoma in Mice.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Li HK, Anko M, Banno K, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Conclusion: 211At-trastuzumab demonstrates potent antitumor efficacy against trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive USC in preclinical models. Targeted α-therapy may represent a promising strategy to overcome resistance to HER2-targeted therapy.

sections.text: Uterine serous carcinoma (USC) is an aggressive endometrial cancer frequently associated with human epidermal growth factor receptor type 2 (HER2) overexpression and poor prognosis. Although trastuzumab improves outcomes, resistance remains a major clinical problem. This study determined whether targeted α-therapy using 211At-labeled trastuzumab (211At-trastuzumab) can overcome trastuzumab resistance in HER2-positive USC. Methods: 211At-trastuzumab was synthesized, and its binding and cytotoxicity in HER2-positive USC cell lines were evaluated. Three trastuzumab-resistant peritoneal metastasis mouse models were established: intrinsic resistance, trastuzumab-induced resistance, and acquired resistance. After a single intravenous administration (1.85 MBq), therapeutic efficacy was assessed using bioluminescence imaging and biodistribution analysis. Results: 211At-trastuzumab showed specific binding to HER2-positive USC cells and significantly reduced cell viability relative to the controls. In vivo, tumor uptake reached 17.4 ± 1.9 %ID/g at 24 h. A single dose significantly suppressed tumor growth in all 3 resistant models: intrinsic, induced, and acquired resistance (P < 0.05 vs. controls). No severe toxicity was observed. Conclusion: 211At-trastuzumab demonstrates potent antitumor efficacy against trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive USC in preclinical models. Targeted α-therapy may represent a promising strategy to overcome resistance to HER2-targeted therapy.

items.title: Clinical Value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Versus [18F]FDG PET/CT for Primary Staging of Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma: Results from a Prospective Northern European Trial.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
items.authors: Bentestuen M, Makieva I, Andersen TB, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

sections.text: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

sections.text: Urethral involvement in IgG4-related disease is rare. We describe FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI findings in a woman with IgG4-related disease presenting as urethral wall thickening with obstructive urinary symptoms. FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI showed significant circumferential thickening of the urethral wall with intense diffuse activity (SUV max , 13) and multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes in pelvic, retroperitoneal, mediastinal, pulmonary hilar, and axillary regions. This case indicates that IgG4-related urethral disease should be included in the differential diagnosis of FDG-avid urethral or periurethral lesions.

sections.text: A 71-year-old woman with a 5-week history of right-sided abdominal pain was initially suspected of hepatobiliary disorders. Upper abdominal ultrasound and MRI revealed unremarkable hepatobiliary findings. Although no hepatobiliary lesions were identified, MRI incidentally detected an ascending colon mass highly suspicious for malignancy. The patient underwent FDG PET/CT for differential diagnosis and preoperative staging. PET/CT with 3D CT reconstruction demonstrated a linear hyperdense foreign body within the ascending colon wall, causing focal bowel wall thickening with intense FDG avidity. These imaging findings were consistent with a foreign body-induced inflammatory granuloma, a diagnosis ultimately confirmed by colonoscopy and biopsy.

sections.text: Bladder diverticula are predisposed to developing intradiverticular bladder tumors. We describe FDG PET/CT findings in a case of intradiverticular bladder cancer. At FDG PET/CT (62 min), the intradiverticular bladder cancer appeared as an exophytic lesion with similar density to the urine in the bladder‌ and intense activity mimicking a bladder diverticulum. At delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT (275 min), the tumor showed higher density and activity than the urine in the bladder, consistent with malignancy. This case indicates that delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT may be necessary for detecting possible intradiverticular bladder cancer in patient with bladder diverticulum.

items.title: Occult Abdominal Para-Aortic Ectopic Insulinoma Localized by 18 F-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT.
items.authors: Wan Y, Wang H, Feng L, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Surgical resection confirmed a solitary ectopic insulinoma, and postoperative hypoglycemia resolved. This case highlights the value of 18 F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT in identifying occult solitary ectopic insulinomas when conventional imaging and surgical exploration are unrevealing, enabling curative resection.

sections.text: Solitary ectopic insulinomas without concurrent pancreatic or gastrointestinal lesions are exceedingly rare. We report the 18 F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT findings of a solitary ectopic insulinoma in a 68-year-old woman with a 10-year history of recurrent hypoglycemic syncope. Endogenous hyperinsulinemia was confirmed, but conventional imaging and laparoscopic pancreatic exploration were negative. PET/CT revealed a solitary intense focus in the para-abdominal aortic region. Surgical resection confirmed a solitary ectopic insulinoma, and postoperative hypoglycemia resolved. This case highlights the value of 18 F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT in identifying occult solitary ectopic insulinomas when conventional imaging and surgical exploration are unrevealing, enabling curative resection.

items.title: A Tale of 3 Tracers: Contrasting Uptake Patterns of 18 F-FDG, 68 Ga-DOTATATE, and 18 F-MFBG in a Pediatric Neuroblastoma Patient.

sections.text: A 5-year-old boy underwent 18 F-FDG PET/CT before the histopathologic diagnosis of neuroblastoma, revealing a metabolically active left adrenal primary tumor with metastases to the liver. Following resection and chemotherapy, sequential 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18 F-MFBG demonstrated tracer-specific uptake patterns: 18 F-MFBG identified a solitary hepatic metastasis undetected by 68 Ga-DOTATATE. This case underscores the complementary diagnostic value of multimodal molecular imaging in pediatric neuroblastoma response assessment.

items.title: Unusual Isolated Thymic Relapse of Neuroblastoma Detected By 123 I-mIBG Scintigraphy in a Pediatric Patient.
items.authors: Chaurasiya K, Kireeva E, Dunaikin M, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: We report a rare case of thymic relapse of NB presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass with intense uptake on 123 I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine ( 123 I-mIBG) scintigraphy. This case highlights an uncommon pattern of NB recurrence and the value of 123 I-mIBG imaging in its detection.

sections.text: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common extracranial solid malignancy of childhood, arising from neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Metastatic spread most frequently involves the bone marrow, bones, lymph nodes, and liver, whereas soft-tissue, central nervous system, and pulmonary metastases are less common. Unusual sites of recurrence may present a significant diagnostic challenge. We report a rare case of thymic relapse of NB presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass with intense uptake on 123 I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine ( 123 I-mIBG) scintigraphy. This case highlights an uncommon pattern of NB recurrence and the value of 123 I-mIBG imaging in its detection.

items.title: A Head-to-Head Comparison of Detection Rate and Tumor Uptake of FAPI, PSMA, and FDG PET/CT in Newly Diagnosed High-risk Prostate Cancer.

conclusion.label: Conclusions

It may improve the detection rate of 68 Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. The clinical value of combining 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: This study was designed to investigate the detection rate and tumor uptake of 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET/CT in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer (PCa), compared with 68 Ga-PSMA-11 and 18 F-FDG PET/CT.

sections.label: Patients and methods
sections.text: This study enrolled 48 patients with biopsy-diagnosed, treatment-naive high-risk PCa who underwent 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, 68 Ga-PSMA-11, and 18 F-FDG PET/CT between April and December 2024. A head-to-head comparison of detection rate and tumor uptake was performed among the 3 tracers. In addition, 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 dual-tracer PET was used to characterize the imaging phenotypes of each lesion and interlesional heterogeneity.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: A total of 477 lesions were detected by the 3 PET tracers. 68 Ga-PSMA-11 exhibited the highest overall detection rate (96.4%), followed by 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI (81.1%) and 18 F-FDG (66.0%). A total of 17 68 Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions were identified in 8 patients, all of which were detected by 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, whereas only 12 were detected by 18 F-FDG. Combined 68 Ga-PSMA-11 and 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET identified all lesions detected by triple-tracer PET. Based on relative tracer dominance of dual-tracer PET, patients were classified as PSMA-dominant (n=23), FAPI-dominant (n=5), or mixed phenotype (n=20). The mixed phenotype with marked interlesional heterogeneity might be associated with more advanced clinical characteristics, with a higher proportion of metastatic disease and a greater metastatic burden.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI is a promising PET tracer for newly diagnosed high-risk PCa. It may improve the detection rate of 68 Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. The clinical value of combining 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

sections.text: A woman in her 50s receiving paclitaxel, carboplatin, and pembrolizumab for recurrent cervical cancer developed herpes zoster and received antiviral therapy. 18 F-FDG PET/CT performed 22 days after zoster onset, when the skin lesions had crusted, demonstrated continuous uptake extending from the left L5 dorsal root ganglion to the sciatic nerve. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of FDG PET findings indicating ganglioneuritis extending from the dorsal root ganglion to a peripheral nerve after herpes zoster. Recognition of this pattern is important in patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy because it may mimic immune-related neuritis or perineural tumor spread.

items.title: The Clinical Significance of Hyperkinetic Biliary Dyskinesia on HIDA Scan: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.authors: Elek A, Bilgin GB, Bilgin C, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: This meta-analysis suggests that a high gallbladder EF in the setting of biliary-type pain could represent clinically relevant hyperkinetic biliary dyskinesia rather than normal physiology. Cholecystectomy appears to provide meaningful symptom relief in appropriately selected patients, and pathologic findings frequently indicate underlying chronic inflammation. Further studies are needed to establish clear diagnostic cutoffs and guide management.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Hyperkinetic biliary dyskinesia, defined as a gallbladder ejection fraction (EF) ≥80% on cholecystokinin (CCK)-stimulated hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid scans in the setting of biliary-type pain, has been increasingly recognized as a potential functional gallbladder disorder. The clinical significance of this entity and the role of cholecystectomy remain uncertain.

sections.label: Patients and methods
sections.text: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting outcomes in patients with CCK-hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid EF ≥80% who underwent cholecystectomy due to non-acute biliary-type pain. Primary outcomes included mean EF, rates of symptom resolution and improvement following cholecystectomy, and prevalence of chronic cholecystitis on pathology. Secondary outcomes included normal histology rates and symptom reproduction with CCK stimulation. All statistical analyses were conducted in R (version 4.5.0) using a random-effects model to obtain pooled estimates.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: A total of 14 retrospective studies, including 686 patients, were analyzed. The pooled mean gallbladder EF was 90.27% (95% CI: 88.73-91.80, I 2 = 86.6%). Symptom resolution occurred in 83.1% (95% CI: 76.7-89.4, I 2 = 76.8%), and symptom improvement in 91.6% (95% CI: 89.0-94.2, I 2 = 29.7%) of patients following cholecystectomy. Histopathologic analysis revealed chronic cholecystitis in 85.1% (95% CI: 76.9-93.4, I 2 = 90.6%) of surgical specimens, while normal gallbladder histology was rare, observed in only 9.9% (95% CI: 4.6-15.2, I 2 = 83.7%). The pooled risk ratio indicated a 6.70-fold higher likelihood of chronic cholecystitis compared with normal histology (95% CI: 3.69-12.17, I 2 = 65.2%, P = 0.0022). Functional reproduction of symptoms during CCK stimulation was frequent, with a pooled rate of 78.3% (95% CI: 70.4-86.3, I 2 = 35.6%). Egger regression test suggested potential publication bias for the normal histology outcome ( P = 0.0223), but not for symptom resolution ( P = 0.1589).

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: This meta-analysis suggests that a high gallbladder EF in the setting of biliary-type pain could represent clinically relevant hyperkinetic biliary dyskinesia rather than normal physiology. Cholecystectomy appears to provide meaningful symptom relief in appropriately selected patients, and pathologic findings frequently indicate underlying chronic inflammation. Further studies are needed to establish clear diagnostic cutoffs and guide management.

sections.text: A 79-year-old man underwent proton beam therapy (PBT) for hepatocellular carcinoma. During follow-up, MRI demonstrated stable T2-weighted hyperintensity in the irradiated region without interval enlargement or mass formation. Five years after PBT, a new hepatocellular carcinoma developed elsewhere in the liver. 18 F-FDG PET showed no apparent abnormal uptake in the irradiated region, whereas 18 F-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-74 PET demonstrated persistent uptake. These findings may reflect chronic radiation-induced fibroinflammatory changes and suggest that fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-PET can visualize such changes even years after PBT.

sections.text: A 3-year-old girl with high-risk neuroblastoma underwent 18 F-MFBG PET/CT for therapy response evaluation as part of a clinical trial. The scan revealed focal increased uptake in the pineal gland, which was also observed on a concurrent 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT. items.title: Dynamic Tc-99m Sulfur Colloid Lymphoscintigraphy With SPECT/CT Revealing a Postrenal Transplant Lymphatic Leak Mimicking Urinoma.

sections.text: 99m Tc sulphur colloid lymphoscintigraphy scan is a safe, noninvasive technique for the visualization of lymphatic pathways in the body. While primarily used to detect lymphatic obstruction, it is also valuable in identifying lymphatic extravasation, guiding targeted treatment strategies. We report a 33-year-old woman who developed a large pelvic fluid collection following renal transplantation, initially misdiagnosed on CT. Dynamic lymphoscintigraphy combined with SPECT/CT accurately identified the etiology and precise anatomic origin of the collection, guiding successful conservative management. This case highlights the complementary role of dynamic lymphoscintigraphy and SPECT/CT in diagnosing unexpected post-transplant complications, where conventional imaging alone may be misleading.

sections.text: 68 Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT is widely used for staging prostate cancer but may also detect nonprostatic malignancies owing to prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) expression in tumor neovasculature. Here, we report a case of a newly diagnosed high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma that underwent staging 68 Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT. In addition to the primary prostatic lesion, PSMA-expressing lesions were identified in the sternum and right thyroid lobe. While skeletal involvement was initially presumed metastatic prostate cancer, further evaluation revealed follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma. This case highlights an important diagnostic pitfall and demonstrates the value of PSMA-PET/CT in uncovering clinically occult synchronous malignancies.

sections.text: Intussusception of bowel in adults is relatively rare and most commonly secondary to gastrointestinal malignancies. We present the case of an 80-year-old man with rectosigmoid adenocarcinoma evaluated via 18 F-FDG PET/CT. Imaging revealed rectosigmoid intussusception with a characteristic "target sign" on both PET and CT images involving the invaginated bowel, alongside synchronous FDG-avid lung metastases. Subsequent MRI confirmed the anatomical findings. This case highlights the unique utility of hybrid 18 F-FDG PET/CT in simultaneously delineating both malignant and nonmalignant metabolic and anatomical changes and providing critical whole-body staging to guide clinical management.

sections.text: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

sections.text: We report a case of a 60-year-old man with biopsy-proven prostate adenocarcinoma who underwent 99m Tc-PSMA scintigraphy during evaluation for potential 177 Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy. The scan demonstrated diffuse skeletal radiotracer accumulation resembling a bone scan. A focal photopenic defect in the thoracic spine corresponded on SPECT/CT to a vertebral hemangioma of the T9 body. An elongated, ventrally deviated (hook-like) xiphoid process, considered a benign anatomic variant, was also identified. This case underscores the importance of recognizing atypical 99m Tc-PSMA distribution patterns and correlating functional with anatomic imaging to avoid misinterpretation and optimize diagnostic accuracy.

sections.text: Gastric metastases from neuroendocrine tumors (NET) are infrequently encountered. Commonly, locally advanced pancreatic NET can involve stomach resulting in inoperable presentation. We herein present a case of gastric wall metastatic disease in postoperative pancreatic NET, which was identified on [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE-PET/CT as recurrence of disease after prolong progression-free period. [18F]F-FDG avidity of the lesions on [18F]F-FDG-PET/CT indicated requirement of chemotherapy alone, or in combination with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). Hence, dual-tracer PET/CT imaging proved important in identifying unusual metastatic disease site and deciding therapeutic strategies in GEP-NET after a long follow-up period following surgical removal of primary disease.

sections.text: A 2-year-old girl was diagnosed with high-risk neuroblastoma. Baseline 18F-MFBG PET/CT demonstrated primary abdominal disease with concurrent multiple metastases. Following induction therapy, restaging 18F-MFBG PET/CT did not show any abnormal 18F-MFBG uptake. However, at six-month follow-up, repeat 18F-MFBG PET/CT revealed multifocal 18F-MFBG-avid lesions confined exclusively to the cranial compartment, with no evidence of extracranial disease recurrence. Subsequent contrast-enhanced brain MRI confirmed the presence of leptomeningeal metastases. This case illustrates that isolated multifocal leptomeningeal metastases may be reliably detected on 18F-MFBG PET/CT, underscoring the utility of this modality in the surveillance of central nervous system involvement in pediatric patients with neuroblastoma.

sections.text: We present [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT findings of an incidentally detected benign phyllodes tumor in a 68-year-old woman with prior colon cancer. Routine contrast-enhanced CT revealed a right breast nodule with moderate enhancement, and subsequent PET/CT demonstrated intense focal FAPI uptake (SUVmax: 6.63). Histology confirmed the presence of a benign phyllodes tumor. This case highlights that FAPI-avid lesions in cancer survivors may represent benign entities with fibroblast-rich stroma, underscoring the importance of considering benign diagnoses and obtaining histologic confirmation to avoid unnecessary treatment.

items.title: Navigating the Pancreatic Duct: Up-to-Date Radiologic Expedition through Intraluminal Pathologic Entities.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Several congenital, traumatic, infectious, inflammatory, and neoplastic processes, as well as iatrogenic interventions, can alter intraluminal contents of the pancreatic duct, leading to adverse outcomes. Variant ductal anatomy may result in clinically significant complications such as duodenal obstruction, acute and chronic pancreatitis, and increased risk of developing gallbladder or biliary malignancies.

sections.text: Several congenital, traumatic, infectious, inflammatory, and neoplastic processes, as well as iatrogenic interventions, can alter intraluminal contents of the pancreatic duct, leading to adverse outcomes. Variant ductal anatomy may result in clinically significant complications such as duodenal obstruction, acute and chronic pancreatitis, and increased risk of developing gallbladder or biliary malignancies. The presence of calculi, blood, pus, and other unintended iatrogenic material in the pancreatic duct can be associated with a range of complications. Neoplastic involvement of the pancreatic duct by entities other than ductal adenocarcinoma is uncommon but may occur secondary to tumor extension into the duct or de novo development. CT and MRI or MR cholangiopancreatography are the most commonly used imaging modalities for evaluating the pancreatic duct and associated pathologic processes. Endoscopic US and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography are more invasive imaging options that also provide the option of simultaneous intervention, if needed. The authors include discussion of the imaging appearances of various congenital anomalies and pathologic processes of the pancreatic duct and complications of ductal disruption and abnormal intraluminal contents. The section on neoplasia provides an up-to-date review of imaging manifestations of recently described neoplastic entities that develop within the pancreatic duct. Awareness of these abnormalities and their imaging correlates may help radiologists improve patient care.

items.title: The relationship between chemical shift MRI findings and histological grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
items.authors: Ozdemir B, Aktan A, Filinte D, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Percentage SI drop was greater in Fuhrman grade 1 than in Fuhrman grades 2-4 ccRCCs, but discrimination was modest and incremental value beyond tumour size was not established. These findings are limited to an exploratory comparison using historical Fuhrman grades and cannot be extrapolated to contemporary World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grading.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of percentage signal intensity (SI) drop on chemical-shift magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for distinguishing Fuhrman grade 1 from Fuhrman grades 2-4 clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective multicenter study included 85 patients with histopathologically confirmed ccRCC who underwent preoperative 1.5-T MRI including chemical-shift sequences between 2016 and 2024. Percentage tumour-to-spleen SI drop was calculated from in-phase and opposed-phase images. Tumours were classified as Fuhrman grade 1 (n = 30) or Fuhrman grades 2-4 (n = 55), based on grades recorded in the original surgical pathology reports. MRI findings were compared between groups, and ROC curve analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminatory performance of percentage SI drop.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Percentage SI drop was significantly greater in Fuhrman grade 1 tumours than in Fuhrman grades 2-4 tumours [40.0% (IQR, 25.4-54.2) vs. 17.4% (IQR, 5.9-29.2); p = 0.003]. Fuhrman grades 2-4 tumours were significantly larger than grade 1 tumours [46 mm (IQR, 28-74) vs. 39 mm (IQR, 30-49); p = 0.01], whereas tumour composition did not differ significantly (p = 0.08). ROC analysis showed modest discriminatory performance (AUC, 0.695; 95% CI, 0.566-0.824; p = 0.003). A percentage SI drop cut-off of ≥ 27.8% yielded 66.7% sensitivity and 67.3% specificity for identifying Fuhrman grade 1 tumours.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Percentage SI drop was greater in Fuhrman grade 1 than in Fuhrman grades 2-4 ccRCCs, but discrimination was modest and incremental value beyond tumour size was not established. These findings are limited to an exploratory comparison using historical Fuhrman grades and cannot be extrapolated to contemporary World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grading.

items.title: Dual-layer spectral CT-derived iodine and extracellular volume biomarkers for noninvasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in Fontan-associated liver disease.
items.authors: Inmutto N, Srisuwan T, Nimitrungtawee N, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In this single-center exploratory study, delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived ECV showed a significant association with histologic fibrosis severity and promising preliminary discrimination for advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis in Fontan-associated liver disease. External validation in larger, independent Fontan cohorts is required before clinical application.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived normalized iodine concentration and extracellular volume fraction for noninvasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in patients with Fontan-associated liver disease.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This single-center exploratory retrospective study included 23 patients with Fontan-associated liver disease who underwent both liver biopsy and delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT between January 2021 and December 2023. Normalized iodine concentration was calculated as hepatic iodine concentration divided by aortic iodine concentration. Hematocrit-adjusted extracellular volume fraction (ECV) was calculated from delayed-phase iodine-density maps. Histologic fibrosis stage based on the METAVIR system was used as the reference standard. Associations between CT biomarkers and fibrosis stage were assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test, and Spearman correlation. Diagnostic performance for advanced fibrosis (≥ F3) and cirrhosis (F4) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Histologic fibrosis stages were F1 in 4 patients, F2 in 2, F3 in 9, and F4 in 8. ECV was higher in advanced fibrosis stages, with median values of 39.21% in F1, 37.15% in F2, 42.72% in F3, and 46.78% in F4. ECV differed significantly among fibrosis stages (p = 0.014), showed a significant ordered trend (p < 0.001), and correlated positively with histologic stage (ρ = 0.666, p < 0.001). IC-normalized showed a weak positive correlation with fibrosis stage, but the ordered trend did not reach statistical significance. For advanced fibrosis, ECV showed promising preliminary discrimination, with an AUC of 0.902 (95% CI, 0.766-1.000). For cirrhosis, ECV showed an AUC of 0.833 (95% CI, 0.655-1.000), with sensitivity of 87.5%, specificity of 80.0%, and negative predictive value of 92.3% at a cutoff of 43.45%.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: In this single-center exploratory study, delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived ECV showed a significant association with histologic fibrosis severity and promising preliminary discrimination for advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis in Fontan-associated liver disease. External validation in larger, independent Fontan cohorts is required before clinical application.

items.title: An interpretable contrast-enhanced CT-based cross-attention transformer model for predicting progression-free survival in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
items.authors: Liu Y, Xu Z, Xia J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The utilization of preoperative CT imaging in a DL framework enabled PFS prediction and risk stratification in patients with MIBC, with potential value for individualized postoperative surveillance.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) typically have a dismal prognosis, even after undergoing radical cystectomy (RC). To address this limitation, we constructed and evaluated a preoperative deep learning (DL) model that leverages computed tomography (CT) imaging to stratify MIBC patients according to their risk of postoperative disease progression.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: Data from MIBC patients undergoing RC at one of four institutions were retrospectively analyzed and allocated to training and validation cohorts. A dual-channel information fusion DL model was developed to predict the postoperative risk of progression according to preoperative CT images. Subsequently, a DL-based clinical signature was created by combining clinical features with the DL-derived score. The concordance index (C-index) and area under the curve (AUC) were used to evaluate the DL model's predictive capability, which was compared with the DL-based clinical signature, a clinical model, and a Ki67 model.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: In the retrospective cohort of 427 patients with MIBC, the DL score demonstrated favorable predictive performance for disease progression in the validation cohort (C-index: 0.774; AUC: 0.785), and generally showed higher predictive performance than the comparator models in the validation cohort. Using an optimal threshold, the patient cohort was categorized into two distinct subgroups, high-risk and low-risk, with differences in the cumulative incidence of progression observed between the two groups, supporting the model's ability to stratify patients according to progression risk.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: The utilization of preoperative CT imaging in a DL framework enabled PFS prediction and risk stratification in patients with MIBC, with potential value for individualized postoperative surveillance.

items.title: CT assessment of colonic laterality in situs inversus and situs ambiguus: a multicenter retrospective study.
items.authors: Kim J, Ham S, Choi G, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Situs inversus usually shows mirror-image colonic laterality and a left-lower-quadrant appendiceal base, but exceptions occur. In this cohort, situs ambiguus showed greater variability. Colonic laterality and appendiceal-base location should be directly assessed on CT rather than inferred from situs classification alone.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To characterize proximal and distal colonic laterality and appendiceal-base location on CT in patients with situs inversus and situs ambiguus.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective multicenter study included 79 patients identified from abdominal CT reports at three tertiary hospitals between December 2003 and March 2025 (70 with situs inversus; 9 with situs ambiguus). A radiologist assessed thoracoabdominal organ arrangement, proximal and distal colonic laterality, combined proximal-distal colonic laterality pattern, and appendiceal-base location. The end of the cecum was used when the appendiceal base was not visible. Distributions of colonic laterality between the two situs types were compared using exact tests.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: In situs inversus, the proximal colon was left-sided in 66/70 patients (94.3%; 95% CI, 86.2-97.8), the distal colon was right-sided in 67/70 (95.7%; 95% CI, 88.1-98.5), and a left-proximal/right-distal combined colonic pattern occurred in 64/70 (91.4%; 95% CI, 82.5-96.0). The appendiceal base or cecal surrogate was in the left lower quadrant in 61/70 (87.1%; 95% CI, 77.3-93.1). In situs ambiguus, the proximal colon was midline-crossing in 7/9 patients (77.8%; 95% CI, 45.3-93.7), and the distal colon was left-sided in 6/9 (66.7%; 95% CI, 35.4-87.9). Locations of the appendiceal base or cecal surrogate were distributed across all abdominal regions. Distributions of segmental and combined colonic laterality differed between situs inversus and situs ambiguus (all exact p < .001).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Situs inversus usually shows mirror-image colonic laterality and a left-lower-quadrant appendiceal base, but exceptions occur. In this cohort, situs ambiguus showed greater variability. Colonic laterality and appendiceal-base location should be directly assessed on CT rather than inferred from situs classification alone.

items.authors: Di Giorgio A, Battisti G, Bonazzi N, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP possess distinct biodistribution profiles precluding direct interchangeability. HMDP maximizes myocardial contrast, whereas DPD provides a superior representation of the systemic musculoskeletal amyloid burden. Nuclear medicine physicians must adopt tracer-specific interpretive approaches to optimize non-invasive phenotyping.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Bone scintigraphy using [99mTc]Tc-DPD or [99mTc]Tc-HMDP is a non-invasive cornerstone for diagnosing transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). However, their interchangeability and the clinical relevance of systemic extracardiac uptake (ExtCU) remain poorly defined.

sections.label: Aim
sections.text: To systematically compare the diagnostic performance and whole-body biodistribution profiles of [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP in patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: We retrospectively evaluated a multicenter cohort of patients investigated for suspected CA who underwent late planar whole-body scintigraphy and targeted SPECT/CT with either radiotracer as part of their diagnostic workup. Inclusion required a final, confirmed diagnosis of ATTRwt, ATTRv, or AL amyloidosis. Myocardial visual Perugini score (VISUAL_PS) and systemic ExtCU (pulmonary, appendicular muscular, visceral, and miscellaneous) were recorded.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The study included 224 patients (DPD: n = 109, comprising 70 ATTRwt, 20 ATTRv, 19 AL; HMDP: n = 115, comprising 90 ATTRwt, 13 ATTRv, 12 AL). In ATTRwt, the DPD cohort presented predominantly with Perugini Grade 2 (76%), whereas the HMDP cohort skewed toward Grade 3 (72%, p < 0.001). DPD was significantly associated with appendicular muscular uptake (ATTRwt: 84% vs. 38%, p < 0.001), creating a competitive "soft-tissue sink effect". Conversely, HMDP demonstrated a unique predilection for pulmonary retention (ATTRwt: 68% vs. 46%, p = 0.008; ATTRv: 61% vs. 10%, p = 0.006). Visceral uptake was rare in ATTR but was a robust negative predictor strongly favoring AL amyloidosis (OR 0.016, p < 0.001).

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP possess distinct biodistribution profiles precluding direct interchangeability. HMDP maximizes myocardial contrast, whereas DPD provides a superior representation of the systemic musculoskeletal amyloid burden. Nuclear medicine physicians must adopt tracer-specific interpretive approaches to optimize non-invasive phenotyping.

sections.label: Trial registration
sections.text: not applicable.

items.title: Machine learning-based CT radiomics for identifying high risk esophageal varices of bleeding in hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.authors: Li PC, Ma CY, Chang SA, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in patients with HCC.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

sections.label: Results
sections.text: In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

items.title: Intraindividual Comparison of Radiation Dose and Image Quality: Photon-counting versus Energy-integrating Detector CT in Obesity.
items.authors: Hegmanns J, Zensen S, Rosok D, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: CTDIvol (median, 11.99 vs 17.05 mGy) and DLP (median, 526.25 vs 709.32 mGy · cm) were lower with PCCT (both P < .001). Conclusion In patients with obesity, intraindividual comparisons demonstrated that PCCT had superior quantitative and subjective image quality at a lower radiation dose than EID CT.

sections.text: Background Maintaining diagnostic CT image quality in patients with obesity remains challenging because increased x-ray attenuation is often offset by higher radiation exposure. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) has demonstrated improved dose efficiency and image quality, but intraindividual data in this population are limited. Purpose To compare radiation dose, quantitative image quality, and subjective image quality between PCCT and energy-integrating detector (EID) CT intraindividually in patients with obesity. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with obesity undergoing thoracic and/or abdominal CT at both PCCT and EID CT between December 1, 2022, and January 31, 2025. Signal, image noise, and signal to noise ratio (SNR) were measured in vascular, parenchymal, muscular, and adipose tissue. Two radiologists independently rated image quality on a six-point Likert scale. Radiation dose parameters were volume CT dose index (CTDIvol), dose-length product (DLP), and effective dose. The paired two-sided t test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for group comparisons. Results This study included 51 patients with obesity (median age, 56 years [IQR, 51-66.5 years]; 33 male). Signal was higher with PCCT than EID CT in vascular structures, parenchymal organs, and muscle and more negative in subcutaneous fat (all P < .001), with similar image noise (P = .09-.84). SNR was higher with PCCT in vascular structures (ascending aorta: mean, 19.65 ± 6.47 [SD] vs 13.22 ± 4.83; P < .001) and most parenchymal organs (liver: 5.53 ± 1.69 vs 4.71 ± 1.89; P = .02). The difference in SNR increased with body mass index for vessels (r = 0.36) and parenchymal organs (r = 0.51) (both P < .001). Both readers rated overall image quality, contrast, and sharpness higher and artifact-related impairment lower for PCCT (all P < .001), whereas subjective image noise was similar (P = .16 and .14). CTDIvol (median, 11.99 vs 17.05 mGy) and DLP (median, 526.25 vs 709.32 mGy · cm) were lower with PCCT (both P < .001). Conclusion In patients with obesity, intraindividual comparisons demonstrated that PCCT had superior quantitative and subjective image quality at a lower radiation dose than EID CT.

items.title: CT-based Node-RADS for standardized evaluation of lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer and its clinicopathological correlates.
items.authors: Xiao X, Jiang F, Chen Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The CT-based Node-RADS demonstrates stability and satisfactory diagnostic performance for identifying patients with lymph node metastasis in treatment-naive RC.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Lymph node metastasis identification has important clinical implications for treatment decision-making in rectal cancer (RC). To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the CT-based Node Reporting and Data System 1.0 (Node-RADS) for lymph node metastasis risk in treatment-naive RC patients, and to investigate the correlation between the Node-RADS score and clinicopathological factors.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: A single-center retrospective study was performed to RC patients (Aug 2020-Dec 2025) who underwent radical resection surgery and preoperative contrast-enhanced CT examination. Lymph node status was assessed using Node-RADS score ranging from 1 to 5. Sensitivity, specificity, and Youden's index were calculated for different Node-RADS cut-off values. The overall diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC). The associations between Node-RADS score and clinicopathological parameters were analyzed.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: A total of 459 RC patients were evaluated, including 174 pN + and 285 pN-. Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 and ≥ 4 have the satisfactory diagnostic performance, with sensitivity/ specificity/Youden's index of 87.36 %/58.25 %/0.46 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 by Reader 1, 89.08 %/54.04 %/0.43 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 by Reader 2, 74.14 %/78.95 %/0.53 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 4 by Reader 1, and 72.99 %/75.44 %/0.48 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 4 by Reader 2, respectively. The AUC of Node-RADS scores were 0.831(95 %CI:0.793-0.864) and 0.806(95 %CI:0.767-0.841) by Reader 1 and Reader 2, respectively. Node-RADS score correlated with pathological T stage, N stage, and lymphovascular invasion. The inter-reader agreement for Node-RADS score were substantial, with weighted kappa values of 0.650.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: The CT-based Node-RADS demonstrates stability and satisfactory diagnostic performance for identifying patients with lymph node metastasis in treatment-naive RC.

items.title: Overuse and False Restraint in Large Language Model Recommendations for Choosing Wisely Scenarios.
items.authors: Ariel D, Endelman S, Laban G

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: The Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Clinicians are increasingly using large language models (LLMs).

sections.label: Objective
sections.text: To evaluate whether commercial LLMs appropriately call for restraint or action from scenarios based on Choosing Wisely recommendations.

sections.label: Design
sections.text: Benchmark evaluation. Fifteen Choosing Wisely recommendations were used to develop 225 scenarios (per recommendation, 10 in which restraint was appropriate and 5 in which action was appropriate). Six commercial LLMs (3 runs each) generated 4050 responses to the 225 scenarios, using a prompt from the clinician perspective.

sections.label: Setting
sections.text: Production application programming interfaces of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google from February to March 2026.

sections.label: Participants
sections.text: No human participants were involved.

sections.label: Measurements
sections.text: Co-primary outcomes were the overuse rate (endorsing action when restraint was appropriate) and the false restraint rate (withholding an appropriate action).

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The rate of LLM-recommended overuse was 5.4% (95% CI, 0.6% to 12.2%); LLMs did not recommend overuse in 8 of 15 recommendations. Two recommendations accounted for most LLM-recommended overuse: thyroid ultrasound for an incidental subcentimeter nodule (overuse recommended in 42.8% of LLM responses) and routine electrocardiography in low-risk adults (overuse recommended in 28.3% of LLM responses). The LLMs recommended overuse in 0.6% to 3.3% of responses for the remaining 5 recommendations. False restraint was rare (0.6% [CI, 0.1% to 1.2%]), was absent for 11 of 15 recommendations, and was highest for prostate-specific antigen screening (3.3%).

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: Single prompts without follow-up; a benchmark rather than real-world use; responses classified by LLM judge with physician adjudication. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: The LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations.

sections.label: Primary funding source
sections.text: None.

items.title: Sequential transarterial radioembolization and atezolizumab plus bevacizumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.authors: Ko Y, Shin H, Hur MH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Sequential TARE-Atezo/Bev may improve survival compared with Atezo/Bev alone in patients with advanced HCC and well-preserved liver function.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: QuestionThe survival benefit of yttrium-90 TARE followed by Atezo/Bev compared with Atezo/Bev alone remains uncertain given limited evidence in advanced HCC. FindingsTARE followed by Atezo/Bev was associated with significantly longer OS than Atezo/Bev alone, with both OS and PFS improved in patients with advanced HCC and preserved liver function. Clinical relevanceSequential TARE followed by Atezo/Bev may offer a survival advantage in selected patients with advanced HCC, supporting the integration of locoregional and systemic therapies.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Yttrium-90 transarterial radioembolization (TARE) combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors has been investigated as a potential therapeutic strategy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, evidence supporting its addition to current standard systemic therapy remains limited. We aimed to compare clinical outcomes in patients with advanced HCC treated with TARE followed by atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (TARE-Atezo/Bev) and Atezo/Bev alone.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This retrospective cohort study included systemic therapy-naïve patients with advanced HCC treated with Atezo/Bev alone or TARE-Atezo/Bev at a single tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025. Baseline characteristics were adjusted using propensity score matching (PSM) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), and the secondary outcome was progression-free survival (PFS).

sections.label: Results
sections.text: A total of 156 eligible patients were enrolled, including 93 in the Atezo/Bev group and 63 in the TARE-Atezo/Bev group. In the unmatched cohort, median OS was significantly longer in the TARE-Atezo/Bev group than in the Atezo/Bev group (14.1 vs 6.4 months; hazard ratio=0.43, 95% confidence interval = 0.29-0.63; p < 0.001), with consistent results after PSM (p = 0.01) and IPTW (p < 0.001). Although PFS was comparable between groups in the overall cohort, patients with Child-Pugh class A (OS: 14.6 vs 7.1 months; PFS: 7.7 vs 6.3 months) or ALBI grade 1 (OS: 21.4 vs 8.3 months; PFS: 8.1 vs 5.7 months) had significantly longer OS and PFS in the TARE-Atezo/Bev group, with similar results after adjustment.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: Sequential TARE-Atezo/Bev may improve survival compared with Atezo/Bev alone in patients with advanced HCC and well-preserved liver function.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: QuestionThe survival benefit of yttrium-90 TARE followed by Atezo/Bev compared with Atezo/Bev alone remains uncertain given limited evidence in advanced HCC. FindingsTARE followed by Atezo/Bev was associated with significantly longer OS than Atezo/Bev alone, with both OS and PFS improved in patients with advanced HCC and preserved liver function. Clinical relevanceSequential TARE followed by Atezo/Bev may offer a survival advantage in selected patients with advanced HCC, supporting the integration of locoregional and systemic therapies.

items.title: Pediatric chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs using deep learning: a multicenter retrospective study.
items.authors: Hwang J, Kim Y, Hwang JY, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Automated age estimation in children is feasible from pelvic radiography using a deep neural network.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Pelvic radiographs are commonly obtained in children, yet their potential for automated chronological age estimation across the full pediatric age range remains unexplored. Findings A deep learning model estimated chronological age from pelvic radiographs with a mean absolute error of 0.394 and 0.513 years on internal and external test sets, respectively. Clinical relevance Deep learning-based chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs is feasible across the full pediatric age range. This approach allows clinically relevant skeletal maturation data to be extracted from imaging already acquired for other indications.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: Pelvic bones exhibit multiple secondary ossification centers during maturation, enabling automated age estimation. This study investigated whether a deep learning model could estimate chronological age from pelvic radiographs across the full pediatric age range.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This retrospective study included pelvic radiographs from two hospitals for model development, from patients aged between 0 and 18 years. A DenseNet161 model was trained to classify age into 19 1-year interval categories using chronological age as a reference standard and conditional ordinal regression (CORN) loss. External validation was conducted using two independent cohorts, including 541 radiographs from a different department of the same hospital and 203 from an external hospital. External validation was performed on 744 radiographs from two independent cohorts. Model performance was evaluated using the accuracy of predictions within 1 year of the chronological age (ACC@dist = 1) and the mean absolute error (MAE).

sections.label: Results
sections.text: A total of 3972 radiographs (median age, 2.5 years; interquartile range, 0-8 years; 2463 males) were included in model development. On the internal test set, the model achieved an MAE of 0.394 years (girls: 0.360; boys: 0.419) and an ACC@dist = 1 of 0.937 (girls: 0.944; boys: 0.931). On the external test sets, the corresponding values were 0.513 years (girls, 0.628; boys, 0.455) and 0.927 (girls, 0.896; boys, 0.943), respectively.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Automated age estimation in children is feasible from pelvic radiography using a deep neural network.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: Question Pelvic radiographs are commonly obtained in children, yet their potential for automated chronological age estimation across the full pediatric age range remains unexplored. Findings A deep learning model estimated chronological age from pelvic radiographs with a mean absolute error of 0.394 and 0.513 years on internal and external test sets, respectively. Clinical relevance Deep learning-based chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs is feasible across the full pediatric age range. This approach allows clinically relevant skeletal maturation data to be extracted from imaging already acquired for other indications.

items.title: Photon-counting computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging in rectal cancer: reassessment of normalized iodine concentration and apparent diffusion coefficient in an expanded cohort.
items.authors: Saeed S, Shahzadi I, Niehoff JH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In this exploratory expanded cohort, lower pretreatment ADC was associated with Dworak grades 0-1. Single-phase portal-venous NIC measured with the described two-dimensional ROI approach did not reproduce the high performance reported in the pilot study and showed no evidence of improved model fit beyond ADC in this cohort. These findings require independent prospective validation.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To reassess pretreatment photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT)-derived normalized iodine concentration (NIC) in an expanded rectal-cancer cohort, using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) as a within-cohort reference marker for histopathologic treatment response.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This single-center retrospective study included 63 patients with rectal adenocarcinoma who underwent pretreatment pelvic MRI and contrast-enhanced PCCT, followed by neoadjuvant treatment and surgical resection. Dworak tumor regression grades 0-1 were classified as poor response (n = 22) and grades 2-4 as moderate/good response (n = 41). MRI and PCCT were performed a median of 3 days apart (IQR, 1-4.5). The previously reported NIC threshold of ≥ 0.36 was reassessed without re-optimization. Twenty-one of 63 patients overlapped with the preceding pilot cohort; therefore, the present study is an expanded reassessment rather than an independent external validation.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Twenty-two patients showed poor response and 41 moderate/good response. ADC interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.959; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90-0.98). In the 61 patients with paired numeric NIC measurements from both observers, NIC interobserver agreement was also excellent (ICC, 0.905; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.858-0.936). Mean ADC was lower in poor responders than in moderate/good responders (0.876 ± 0.186 vs. 1.035 ± 0.208 × 10⁻³ mm²/s; p = 0.003; AUC, 0.738; 95% CI, 0.608-0.867). NIC did not differ between groups (median, 0.313 vs. 0.370; p = 0.91; AUC, 0.509; 95% CI, 0.362-0.656). Applying the previously published NIC threshold ≥ 0.36 yielded sensitivity 53.7%, specificity 63.6%, and accuracy 57.1% for Dworak grades 2-4. Adding NIC to ADC did not improve model fit (likelihood-ratio p = 0.601).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: In this exploratory expanded cohort, lower pretreatment ADC was associated with Dworak grades 0-1. Single-phase portal-venous NIC measured with the described two-dimensional ROI approach did not reproduce the high performance reported in the pilot study and showed no evidence of improved model fit beyond ADC in this cohort. These findings require independent prospective validation.

items.title: Structured MRI reporting for deep pelvic endometriosis: objective report quality and surgeon-perceived clinical utility in a randomized comparative study.
items.authors: Burgart L, Host A, Gabriele V, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Structured MRI reporting was associated with higher objective completeness and, in an exploratory assessment, higher surgeon ratings for several dimensions of perceived clinical utility. These findings should be balanced against longer reporting time and more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To compare structured and free-text MRI reporting in terms of objective report quality and surgeon ratings of perceived clinical utility in suspected deep pelvic endometriosis.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: In this single-center randomized reader study, 20 radiology residents were assigned to free-text or structured reporting. Five residents became unavailable before report generation and provided no outcome data. The remaining 15 readers completed the same 22 pelvic MRI examinations, generating 330 reports: 154 free-text and 176 structured reports. Reports were compared with an imaging reference standard established by two pelvic radiologists through independent review and consensus adjudication. The primary endpoint was clinically weighted completeness. Secondary endpoints included unweighted completeness, explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference, positive findings unsupported by the expert imaging reference, and reporting time. Objective outcomes were analyzed using mixed-effects models or Poisson generalized estimating equations. In an exploratory paired assessment, two expert gynecologic surgeons evaluated 44 reports, comprising one free-text and one structured report for each MRI examination.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Structured reporting was associated with an 8.1%-point increase in completeness compared with free-text reporting (95% CI, 4.1-12.1; p < 0.001) and a 5.6%-point increase in clinically weighted completeness (95% CI, 1.3-10.0; p = 0.011). Reporting time was 4.52 min longer with structured reporting (95% CI, 3.05-5.99; p < 0.001). Structured reporting was also associated with more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference (rate ratio, 2.94; 95% CI, 1.73-4.98; p < 0.001). These discrepancies were mainly explicit compartment-based negative statements. In the exploratory surgeon assessment, structured reports received higher ratings for perceived completeness, usefulness for clinical decision-making, and adequacy to clinical needs, whereas clarity ratings were similar between formats.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Structured MRI reporting was associated with higher objective completeness and, in an exploratory assessment, higher surgeon ratings for several dimensions of perceived clinical utility. These findings should be balanced against longer reporting time and more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference.

items.title: Radiological lymphoceles and clinically relevant lymphatic complications after retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for testicular cancer: a longitudinal imaging study.
items.authors: Lenart S, Wafa H, Pichler U, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Lymphoceles are frequently detected by routine serial imaging after PC-RPLND but rarely translate into clinically relevant lymphatic morbidity. Radiologically detected lymphoceles should therefore be distinguished from clinically relevant lymphatic complications when interpreting surveillance imaging, counselling patients, and reporting postoperative outcomes after RPLND.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: Postoperative lymphoceles are recognized complications of retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) for testicular germ cell tumours (TGCT). Previous studies have predominantly reported symptomatic or intervention-requiring lymphoceles, whereas the incidence, temporal evolution, and clinical relevance of lymphoceles on postoperative imaging remain poorly defined. We evaluated radiologically detected lymphoceles and clinically relevant lymphatic complications after post-chemotherapy RPLND (PC-RPLND) using routine serial imaging.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 86 consecutive patients who underwent PC-RPLND under a standardized perioperative management protocol. Postoperative imaging consisted of ultrasound at postoperative day 5-7 and 3-4 weeks, followed by computed tomography at 3 and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the incidence of any imaging-detected lymphocele during follow-up. Secondary endpoints included lymphocele prevalence at each imaging time point, clinically relevant lymphatic complications, postoperative complications, and exploratory factors associated with lymphocele formation.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Of 86 included patients, 85 were evaluable for the primary endpoint. Overall, 46 patients (54.1%) had at least one imaging-detected lymphocele during follow-up. Lymphoceles were most frequently detected at discharge (36/84, 42.9%) and decreased over time to 32.8% (19/58) at 3-4 weeks, 31.5% (17/54) at 3 months, and 15.8% (9/57) at 12 months. Clinical follow-up was available for 65 patients. Clinically relevant lymphatic complications occurred in only 3 patients (4.6%), comprising two cases of lymphatic/chylous ascites and one lymphatic fistula associated with a small precaval lymphocele. Among 49 patients with paired 3- and 12-month CT, 10 of 16 lymphoceles present at 3 months had resolved by 12 months, whereas only one was newly detected (exact McNemar p = .012). Exploratory analyses identified no significant associations between imaging-detected lymphocele formation and patient characteristics, tumour-related factors, surgical approach, or extent of lymphadenectomy.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: Lymphoceles are frequently detected by routine serial imaging after PC-RPLND but rarely translate into clinically relevant lymphatic morbidity. Radiologically detected lymphoceles should therefore be distinguished from clinically relevant lymphatic complications when interpreting surveillance imaging, counselling patients, and reporting postoperative outcomes after RPLND.

items.title: Photon counting detector CTA for prostate arterial evaluation during the workup for prostate artery embolization.
items.authors: Linch F, Rajiah P, Jundt M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Small FOV UHR PCD CTA is useful in identifying candidate PA supply, as well as potential extraprostatic anastomoses, providing an arterial roadmap for PAE planning. Candidate PA supply was confirmed by DSA in all selected vessels among patients who proceeded to PAE.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To evaluate small field of view (FOV) ultra-high spatial resolution pelvic photon-counting detector prostate CT angiograms (UHR PCD CTA) for identifying prostate arterial anatomy and extraprostatic anastomoses in patients undergoing workup for prostate artery embolization (PAE).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: IRB-approved retrospective imaging and electronic medical record review of men who consecutively underwent UHR PCD CTA for PAE workup at our institution from 8/1/2022 to 12/1/2024. UHR PCD CTAs were evaluated by two vascular and interventional radiologists for main and accessory candidate prostatic arteries (PA/s) and anastomoses to penile, bladder, or rectal arteries. A main PA was defined as supplying the central gland and an accessory PA was defined as supplying the peripheral zone. PAs were categorized using the Carnevale classification. In patients who proceeded to PAE, digital subtraction angiograms (DSA) were retrospectively compared with UHR PCD CTA findings.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: UHR PCD CTA was obtained prior to PAE consultation for 50 men. We evaluated 100 pelvic sides, identifying 180 candidate PAs with a median of 3 candidate PAs per patient (mean, 3.6; range, 2-7). Overall, 56% (101/180) of candidate PAs were main and 44% (79/180) were accessory. Abridged Carnevale classifications: Type 5-21% (38/180). Eight accessory candidate PAs arose from the superior rectal artery. At least one candidate anastomosis arose from 40% (72/180) of candidate PAs. Of 95 total candidate anastomoses, 69 were extraprostatic (30 rectal, 20 bladder, 19 penile) and 26 were intraprostatic collaterals; 56% (53/95) arose from accessory and 44% (42/95) from main candidate PAs. Twenty-eight of 50 (56%) men underwent PAE, during which 72% (74/103) of available candidate PAs were selected, and prostatic supply was confirmed by DSA in 100% (74/74) of selected vessels.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Small FOV UHR PCD CTA is useful in identifying candidate PA supply, as well as potential extraprostatic anastomoses, providing an arterial roadmap for PAE planning. Candidate PA supply was confirmed by DSA in all selected vessels among patients who proceeded to PAE.

items.title: Deep learning super-resolution enhances MRI radiomics for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and invasiveness.
items.authors: Yang CZ, Qin LH, Chen L, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) is a severe obstetric complication. This study evaluated whether retrospective, post-processing deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction (SR) was associated with improved MRI radiomics performance for predicting PAS and invasive PAS.

sections.label: Materials & methods
sections.text: This retrospective study involved 245 patients who had placental MRI scans at three different institutions. Of these, 158 cases from Institution I for training set and internal validation set, while 34 patients from Institution II and 53 patients from Institution III served as external validation sets. SR using a generative adversarial network (GAN) was applied to generate SR T2WI (SRT2WI). Predictive models for PAS and invasive PAS were developed based on T2WI, SRT2WI, and the SRT2WI-Clinical model. Two radiologists independently diagnosed PAS using T2WI to serve as a reference for evaluating model performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), Delong test, and net reclassification improvement (NRI). SHAP values interpreted the models and quantified feature contributions.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Across all four cohorts, SRT2WI yielded numerically higher AUCs than T2WI, and SRT2WI-Clinical achieved the highest AUCs. For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

items.title: Deep learning reconstruction in prostate MRI: technical principles, clinical applications, and future directions.
items.authors: Virk MS, Rajamohan N, Bagga B, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has become integral to the detection, localization, risk stratification, and management of prostate cancer. sections.text: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has become integral to the detection, localization, risk stratification, and management of prostate cancer. Increasing utilization of prostate MRI in screening, active surveillance, targeted biopsy guidance, and treatment planning has amplified the demand for faster imaging protocols while maintaining high diagnostic quality. Conventional MRI acceleration strategies, including parallel imaging and compressed sensing, improve acquisition efficiency but remain limited by trade-offs involving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), image sharpness, artifacts, and reconstruction complexity. Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) has emerged as a promising artificial intelligence-based approach for MRI acceleration and image enhancement. Unlike traditional reconstruction methods that rely primarily on predefined mathematical models, DLR uses neural networks to learn image priors and reconstruction features from MRI data. Published studies suggest that DLR may enable accelerated acquisitions while maintaining or, in some settings, improving image quality through denoising, artifact reduction, and improved spatial resolution and lesion conspicuity. However, these effects vary according to the reconstruction algorithm, sequence, acceleration factor, and clinical setting. Variational networks combine physics-based MRI constraints with learned regularization and represent an important framework for DLR. In prostate MRI, available studies have reported substantial reductions in acquisition time for T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging while generally maintaining perceived image quality. Reported benefits include improved lesion conspicuity, reader confidence, and delineation of anatomic structures. Current evidence suggests that DLR generally preserves PI-RADS assessment and diagnostic performance rather than systematically altering lesion categorization; however, evidence demonstrating improvements in diagnostic accuracy or clinical outcomes remains limited. Important limitations include vendor and algorithm dependence, potential reconstruction artifacts, variability in quantitative imaging metrics, limited multicenter validation, and uncertain generalizability across scanners, protocols, and clinical settings. This review summarizes the technical principles underlying DLR, discusses current clinical applications in prostate MRI, highlights representative studies and workflow implications, reviews limitations, and outlines future directions for this rapidly evolving technology.
