items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Prostate Cancer Detection and Screening on MRI in Global Populations: The SCARLET-1 Study.
items.authors: Saha A, Bosma JS, Twilt JJ, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Subgroup performance was consistent across age, risk, cancer location and ethnicity (mean ΔAUC, 0.02), but varied substantially across 25 sites (28% with AUC<0.80; 32% with AUC ≥0.90) and by image quality (AUC, 0.78-0.88). Conclusion AI demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of radiology readings across external diagnostic and screening datasets.

sections.text: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have demonstrated non-inferiority to radiologists for prostate cancer detection on MRI, but evidence in global diagnostic and population-based screening settings remains limited. Purpose To determine whether an AI system can achieve diagnostic performance comparable to radiology readings for detecting Gleason grade group ≥2 prostate cancer on MRI in external diagnostic and screening datasets. Materials and Methods In the SCARLET-1 retrospective validation study, prostate MRIs from adults with suspected prostate cancer (January 2012-October 2024) were used to evaluate an AI system, with external testing in diagnostic (PRIME) and organized screening settings (STHLM3-MRI and IP1-PROSTAGRAM). The primary outcome was agreement between AI assessments and standard-of-care diagnoses of Gleason grade group ≥2 cancer, with diagnostic interchangeability defined relative to the estimated agreement of an average radiologist. Secondary outcomes included area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across datasets and subgroups. Results 22,445 examinations (21,252 male patients; median age, 66 years [IQR 60-71]) were included: 20,471 prostate MRI examinations (19,278 patients; 26 cities, 14 countries) for AI training and internal testing, and 1974 patients (20 external cities, 12 countries) for external testing. External AUCs were 0.86 (95% CI: 0.83, 0.90) in PRIME, 0.89 (95% CI: 0.86, 0.92) in STHLM3-MRI, and 0.84 (95% CI: 0.70, 0.95) in IP1-PROSTAGRAM. The primary outcome was 83.0% (395 of 476; adjusted 95% CI: 78.8%, 87.0%), 87.9% (974 of 1108; adjusted 95% CI: 85.6%, 90.3%), and 87.7% (342 of 390; adjusted 95% CI: 83.6%, 91.5%), respectively, meeting prespecified interchangeability criteria in all datasets. Subgroup performance was consistent across age, risk, cancer location and ethnicity (mean ΔAUC, 0.02), but varied substantially across 25 sites (28% with AUC<0.80; 32% with AUC ≥0.90) and by image quality (AUC, 0.78-0.88). Conclusion AI demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of radiology readings across external diagnostic and screening datasets.

items.title: 177Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Prior to Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy in Oligorecurrent Prostate Cancer: Secondary and Exploratory End Point Results from the Randomized Phase 2 LUNAR Trial.
items.authors: Kishan AU, Wilhalme H, Felix C, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

sections.text: The phase 2 randomized LUNAR trial previously demonstrated that neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (orHSPC). We report updated efficacy and safety outcomes with extended follow-up. Patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-detected orHSPC and one to five metastatic lesions amenable to SBRT were randomized 1:1 to SBRT alone or two cycles of neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 followed by SBRT. The primary end point was PFS, defined as new lesions on PSMA PET/CT, initiation of salvage hormonal therapy, or death. Secondary end points included hormonal therapy-free survival (HT-FS) and 24-mo progression-free status. Exploratory end points included polymetastatic PFS (poly-PFS), castration-resistant disease-free survival (CRFS), and conventional imaging progression-free survival (CT-PFS). Between September 2022 and November 2023, 92 patients were randomized to SBRT alone (n = 47) or 177Lu-PNT2002 plus SBRT (n = 45). At a median follow-up of 31.9 mo, 177Lu-PNT2002 significantly improved PFS (median 17.6 vs 7.4 mo; hazard ratio [HR] 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.23-0.61; p < 0.001) and HT-FS (HR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.34-0.95; p = 0.03). Exploratory analyses demonstrated improved poly-PFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI = 0.08-1.03; p = 0.04), CRFS (HR 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02-1.10; p = 0.03), and CT-PFS (HR 0.46, 95% CI = 0.19-1.09; p = 0.07). No new safety signals were observed. With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

items.title: Associations between tissue stiffness, tumor response to transarterial chemoembolization and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: insights from multifrequency 3D-magnetic resonance elastography.
items.authors: Chen J, Zhang Z, Ye Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

sections.label: Objectives
sections.text: To investigate the correlation between tissue stiffness, as measured across various target tissues using multifrequency three-dimensional magnetic resonance elastography (3D-MRE), and tumor responses to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), as well as post-treatment prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: HCC patients scheduled for TACE treatment were prospectively recruited and received multifrequency 3D-MRE before the initiation of TACE procedure. Measurements of tumor stiffness (TS), liver stiffness (LS), and spleen stiffness (SS) were conducted at frequencies of 60 Hz and 30 Hz, respectively. Treatment response was assessed using the mRECIST. Patient follow-up was conducted to evaluate overall survival outcomes.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The final patient cohort consisted of 43 patients (mean age: 56.66±10.13 years; 34 males), including 16 non-responders and 27 responders. Non-responders exhibited significantly elevated TS (4.10±2.54 vs. 2.68±1.61kPa, p=0.035), LS (2.88±1.43 vs. 1.97±0.59kPa, p=0.026), and SS (4.03±0.90 vs. 3.13±1.08kPa, p=0.008) at the frequency of 30Hz. Firth's penalized univariable logistic analysis identified age (adjusted odds ratio [OR]=0.93, P=0.036), tumor number (OR=0.69, P=0.035), LS at 60Hz (OR=0.79, p=0.046), TS at 30Hz (OR=0.73, p=0.037), LS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, p=0.008), and SS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, P=0.009) as potential predictors of treatment response. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for predicting treatment response was 0.69 for age, tumor number and TS at 30Hz, 0.67 for LS at both 60Hz and 30Hz, and 0.75 for SS at 30Hz. Univariable Cox regression identified TS at both 60Hz (hazard ratio=1.15, p=0.014) and 30Hz (hazard ratio=1.40, p=0.010) as potential predictors of overall survival.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

items.title: CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.authors: Tan Y, Xu S, Liu X, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Nuclear β-catenin accumulation reflects activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but noninvasive preoperative prediction of this immunohistochemical phenotype remains incompletely established.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To develop and externally validate CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) models for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This multicenter retrospective study included 1029 patients with histopathologically confirmed HCC. Patients from two participating institutions formed the development cohort and were split into training (n=620; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 293) and internal validation (n=267; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 126) sets. Patients from an independent third institution formed the external validation cohort (n=142; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 43). Whole-tumor portal venous phase CT radiomics features and topology-based ITH features were extracted from the audited image-mask cohort. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using AUC, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, calibration summaries, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: In external validation, AUCs were 0.677 for the clinical model, 0.862 for the radiomics model, 0.857 for the ITH model, 0.831 for the core ITH model, 0.863 for the radiomics-ITH model, and 0.886 for the stacking model. Compared with radiomics alone, stacking showed a numerical ΔAUC of 0.024 (95% CI, -0.010 to 0.060; P=0.180).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

items.title: Development and validation of a preoperative CT-based radiomics nomogram for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis after pancreatoduodenectomy.
items.authors: Chen H, Sun L, Liu J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To investigate the value of radiomics based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis (PPAP) after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: A retrospective analysis included 104 patients who underwent PD and preoperative CECT between May 2019 and March 2025. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 73) and test (n = 31) sets at a 7:3 ratio. PPAP was defined according to the biochemical and radiologic components of the International Study Group for Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) criteria. After pancreatic parenchyma delineation, radiomics feature extraction and selection, an optimal model was developed on the training set to calculate the radiomics score (rad-score). Independent clinical and morphological features were selected by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Conventional quantitative CT attenuation ratios of the pancreatic parenchyma were also evaluated. Predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: PPAP occurred in 41 patients. Four models were compared: a clinical-morphologic model (age and main pancreatic duct [MPD] dilation), a conventional model (age, MPD dilation and arterial-to-portal ratio [A/P]), a radiomics model (rad-score alone), and a radiomics-integrated model (age, MPD dilation and rad-score). The radiomics-integrated model achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) among the four models, with the AUC of 0.854 (95% CI 0.758-0.951) in the training set and 0.862 (95% CI 0.732-0.993) in the test set.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

items.title: MRI-derived radiomics for prostate cancer active surveillance: a systematic review.
items.authors: Kyle ET, Sweeney KJ, McCabe DH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Progression endpoints were heterogeneous and several were of limited clinical relevance. A core outcome set for AS (at least ISUP grade group ≥3 and/or unequivocal radiological progression), followed by multi-centre external validation with a head-to-head comparison against the PRECISE v2 (Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation) score, is the priority before clinical use can be considered.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To systematically review MRI-derived radiomic and artificial intelligence models predicting outcomes in men on or eligible for active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer, and whether reported endpoints permit quantitative synthesis.

sections.label: Method
sections.text: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science (2000-September 2026). Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (QUADAS-2, PROBAST) and methodological quality (METRICS). Three subgroups were defined: AS selection at diagnosis, baseline detection of clinically significant cancer, and progression during follow-up. Pooling was pre-specified for subgroups with at least four independent cohorts; endpoint equivalence was assessed.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Seventeen studies across 12 unique cohorts were included. Seven publications derived from two cohorts; 12 independent cohort-level estimates (n = 2703) remained after overlap resolution. Nine publications (four independent cohorts) addressed progression (AUC 0.70 to 0.95), but progression was defined in five non-equivalent ways, from any grade-group increase to composite core-count criteria, precluding quantitative synthesis. Risk of bias was high or unclear in 16 of 17 studies; the median METRICS score was 32.3 % (range 18.9-52.3 %). No study reported external validation or calibration for progression.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: Progression endpoints were heterogeneous and several were of limited clinical relevance. A core outcome set for AS (at least ISUP grade group ≥3 and/or unequivocal radiological progression), followed by multi-centre external validation with a head-to-head comparison against the PRECISE v2 (Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation) score, is the priority before clinical use can be considered.

items.title: Multiparametric MRI assessment of renal Masses: Diagnostic performance of the modified clear cell likelihood score and ancillary MRI features.
items.authors: Asfuroğlu U, Cindil E, Kalafat B, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Incorporation of pseudocapsule assessment into the ccLS improved differentiation between benign and malignant renal masses while maintaining comparable diagnostic performance for identifying ccRCC. T2 SI ratio may provide additional value in MRI-based characterization of renal masses.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance and interreader agreement of the Clear Cell Likelihood Score (ccLS), the modified Clear Cell Likelihood Score (m-ccLS), and ancillary MRI features for differentiating benign from malignant renal masses and clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) from non-ccRCC lesions.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: This retrospective single-center study included 106 patients with renal masses who underwent multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) between 2018 and 2026. MRI features, including T1 signal intensity (SI) ratio, T2 SI ratio, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) ratio, and arterial-to-delayed enhancement ratio (ADER), were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis in both the overall cohort and the cT1a subgroup. Two radiologists independently assigned ccLS and m-ccLS scores and assessed the presence of a pseudocapsule for interreader agreement analysis.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Among 106 renal masses, 73 (68.9 %) were classified as cT1a tumors. For differentiating benign from malignant renal masses, m-ccLS demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than ccLS in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.770 vs. 0.654) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.784 vs. 0.689). For differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC lesions, ccLS and m-ccLS showed comparable diagnostic performance in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.884 vs. 0.868) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.885 vs. 0.876). Among the evaluated ancillary MRI features, the T2 SI ratio was significantly associated with both benign-malignant discrimination and ccRCC identification. Interreader agreement for ccLS, m-ccLS, and pseudocapsule assessment was substantial.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Incorporation of pseudocapsule assessment into the ccLS improved differentiation between benign and malignant renal masses while maintaining comparable diagnostic performance for identifying ccRCC. T2 SI ratio may provide additional value in MRI-based characterization of renal masses.

items.title: Utility of PSA density velocity in diagnosing prostate cancer on prostate MR.
items.authors: Narayanasamy S, Kurata Y, Kido A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Higher PSAD-velocity was associated with presence of csPCa on univariate analysis but not on multivariate analysis, and on fixed-model analysis did not meaningfully improve diagnostic discrimination beyond established predictors.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To assess if PSA density (PSAD) velocity is a predictor of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: Patients undergoing prostate MR for suspected csPCa between 2017 and 2023 were included. Of these, patients who underwent two or more MR exams within 0.3 to 2 years to each other and pathological confirmation within 1 year after the last MR were identified. PI-RADS score, patient age, no-prior-PCa cohort or active surveillance (AS), PSA, PSAD, PSA-velocity and PSAD-velocity were assessed if they were predictor of csPCa. For univariate analysis, all variables were assessed using student t or chi-square tests. When variables were considered significant, variables were entered into multivariate logistic regression model. To assess whether PSAD-velocity adds diagnostic value beyond established predictors, we compared a base model (age, PI-RADS score, clinical cohort, and current PSAD) with the same model plus PSAD-velocity, using optimism-corrected AUC from 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: 23,244 MRs were performed (17,703 for no-prior-PCa, 5,541 for AS). 1,174 patients (mean age: 65.9 years) met the inclusion criteria, and 550 (46.8%) were diagnosed with csPCa. On univariate analysis, PI-RADS score (p<.0001), age (67.0 vs. 64.9 years, p<.0001), AS status (67% vs. 59%, p = .004), PSA (7.5 vs. 6.6 ng/mL, p<.001), PSAD (p<.0001), and PSAD-velocity (0.023 vs. 0.012 ng/mL/mL/year, p = .005) were associated with csPCa, but PSA-velocity (1.4 vs. 1.2 ng/mL/year, p=.38) was not. On multivariable analysis, PI-RADS score (p<.0001), age (p<.0001), AS status (p = .002), PSA (p<.0001), and PSAD (p<.0001) remained significant predictors, but PSAD-velocity was not (p = .13). Adding PSAD-velocity to the base model produced no significant improvement in optimism-corrected AUC (0.7605 vs. 0.7611; ΔAUC = + 0.0006, 95% CI -0.0002 to +0.0019).

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: Higher PSAD-velocity was associated with presence of csPCa on univariate analysis but not on multivariate analysis, and on fixed-model analysis did not meaningfully improve diagnostic discrimination beyond established predictors.

items.title: Abdominal hydatid disease and its mimics: a comprehensive pictorial review of imaging clues to the differential diagnosis.
items.authors: Shabana A, Elkasabi AY, Neimatallah M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Recognizing the characteristic imaging features of HD and its mimics is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate management. A systematic approach that incorporates lesion morphology, organ involvement, disease stage, and relevant clinical and epidemiological information can improve diagnostic confidence, enable early diagnosis, and help avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate intervention.

sections.label: Background
sections.text: Hydatid disease (HD), also known as echinococcosis, is a parasitic disease caused by tapeworms. HD is endemic in many parts of the world and can affect virtually any organ system. Due to the rapid growth of worldwide migration, especially in recent decades, the disease can be diagnosed anywhere, particularly among immigrants in non-endemic areas.

sections.label: Objective
sections.text: To illustrate the spectrum of abdominal imaging manifestations of HD and to review the principal benign and malignant abdominal cystic lesions that can mimic HD, using an organ-based approach with emphasis on imaging features that aid in differential diagnosis.

sections.label: Findings
sections.text: Radiologic imaging is crucial for diagnosing HD, assessing disease activity, progression, and complications, and detecting stage- and organ-specific features. Hydatid disease in the abdomen can mimic other abdominal diseases, depending on the organ involved. Additionally, many other abdominal lesions can mimic hydatid disease and present with similar clinical symptoms. This pictorial review demonstrates characteristic imaging findings of HD and its mimics across the different abdominal organs and spaces, highlighting specific morphological features and potential diagnostic pitfalls. This review incorporates the World Health Organization Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE) classification to provide a standardized framework for describing the imaging appearances of cystic echinococcosis.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Recognizing the characteristic imaging features of HD and its mimics is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate management. A systematic approach that incorporates lesion morphology, organ involvement, disease stage, and relevant clinical and epidemiological information can improve diagnostic confidence, enable early diagnosis, and help avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate intervention.

items.title: The diagnostic value of high-resolution 3D T2-weighted MRI in preoperative evaluation and classification of Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome: a prospective study.
items.authors: Qi Y, Song S, Gao X, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: High-resolution 3D T2 MRI is superior to conventional T2 TSE sequences in the preoperative evaluation of HWWS, especially for identifying communications and precisely locating obstruction sites.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Accurate preoperative structural assessment and classification of HWWS are clinically essential, yet conventional MRI has limitations in identifying fine anatomical structures and small communications. Findings High-resolution 3D T2 MRI outperforms conventional T2 TSE in identifying vaginal and cervical communications and precisely localizing obstruction sites in preoperative evaluation of HWWS. Critical relevance statement This study supports routine inclusion of 3D sequences in HWWS imaging protocols. Combined with renal and spinal assessment, it provides a comprehensive preoperative evaluation that enhances surgical planning precision and optimizes patient management strategies.

sections.label: Objective
sections.text: Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS) is a rare female reproductive tract malformation. Accurate preoperative diagnosis and classification are vital for surgical planning. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic value of high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) T2-weighted MRI in the preoperative assessment and classification of HWWS.

sections.label: Materials and methods
sections.text: The study prospectively enrolled 84 patients clinically diagnosed with HWWS between May 2020 and January 2025. Seventy patients underwent pelvic MRI examinations, including high-resolution 3D T2 sequences (1 mm slice thickness) and conventional T2 TSE sequences, supplemented by large-field-of-view (FOV) T2 coronal imaging for urinary system evaluation and full-spine X-ray examinations for skeletal assessment. Two experienced radiologists independently evaluated the imaging features in a blinded manner, focusing on uterine morphology, obstruction sites, presence of communications, and related anomalies and complications. Consistency analysis was performed between imaging findings and surgical results in 52 surgical patients.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Uterine morphology included: didelphys (54/70, 77.1%), complete septate (14/70, 20%), and bicornuate uterus (2/70, 2.9%). Among 52 surgical patients, 31 (59.6%) had vaginal-level obstruction with 18 (34.6%) Type I, 11 (21.2%) Type II, and 2 (3.8%) Type III, and 21 (40.4%) had cervical-level obstruction (Type IV and mixed). 3D T2 sequences identified 7 (63.6%) vaginal septum fistulas, outperforming TSE sequences, which detected none (0%) (p = 0.005). Associated findings were ipsilateral renal agenesis (98.6%), ovarian endometriosis (22.9%), hematosalpinx (22.9%), and spinal abnormalities (scoliosis (25.7%), mild scoliosis (41.4%).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: High-resolution 3D T2 MRI is superior to conventional T2 TSE sequences in the preoperative evaluation of HWWS, especially for identifying communications and precisely locating obstruction sites.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: Question Accurate preoperative structural assessment and classification of HWWS are clinically essential, yet conventional MRI has limitations in identifying fine anatomical structures and small communications. Findings High-resolution 3D T2 MRI outperforms conventional T2 TSE in identifying vaginal and cervical communications and precisely localizing obstruction sites in preoperative evaluation of HWWS. Critical relevance statement This study supports routine inclusion of 3D sequences in HWWS imaging protocols. Combined with renal and spinal assessment, it provides a comprehensive preoperative evaluation that enhances surgical planning precision and optimizes patient management strategies.

items.title: Near-complete Response of Bilateral Adrenal Metastases to 177Lu-PSMA Therapy in Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer on Posttherapeutic SPECT-CT Follow Up.
items.authors: Yilmaz B, Ozkanli G, Özcan E, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: As the patient was oligometastatic, refractory to previous systemic therapies, and ineligible for surgery or radiotherapy, 177Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy was initiated. After four treatment cycles, PSA levels progressively decreased, and post-therapeutic follow-up SPECT/CT demonstrated a near-complete response in adrenal and bone metastases without treatment-related adverse effects.

sections.text: A 72-year-old man with castration-resistant prostate adenocarcinoma underwent 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for restaging due to significantly increased PSA levels during chemotherapy. Imaging revealed high 68Ga-PSMA-11 uptake in bilateral adrenal uptake, with additional uptake in the prostate and few sclerotic bone lesions. MRI and afterwards adrenal gland biopsy confirmed adrenal metastases, an uncommon metastatic site. As the patient was oligometastatic, refractory to previous systemic therapies, and ineligible for surgery or radiotherapy, 177Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy was initiated. After four treatment cycles, PSA levels progressively decreased, and post-therapeutic follow-up SPECT/CT demonstrated a near-complete response in adrenal and bone metastases without treatment-related adverse effects.

items.title: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT Detection of Hypertrophic Osteoarthropathy in a Pediatric Patient With Neuroblastoma Following Anti-GD2 Immunotherapy.
items.authors: Li S, Wang X, Zhang K, et al.

sections.text: A 5-year-old boy with high-risk neuroblastoma underwent 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT as part of a clinical trial to assess treatment response after anti-GD2 immunotherapy. The scan showed symmetric increased uptake in bilateral femora and tibiae with periostosis. 18F-MFBG PET/CT revealed no abnormal uptake, and no metastasis was found. The diagnosis was hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. This case demonstrates that hypertrophic osteoarthropathy can occur as a rare complication after anti-GD2 therapy and can be detected by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

sections.text: Localized intrahepatic bile duct dilatation (LIBD) is a prevalent radiological finding characterized by a variety of etiologies, including congenital anomalies, inflammatory conditions, hepatolithiasis, and neoplastic lesions. Accurate differential diagnosis of diseases associated with LIBD is crucial for formulating appropriate treatment strategies and improving patient prognosis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the definitions, etiologies, clinical symptoms, and key imaging features of common diseases associated with LIBD. Furthermore, it proposes a structured approach for differential diagnosis. By integrating imaging findings with clinical and laboratory data, this approach aims to improve diagnostic accuracy and assist radiologists in making optimal clinical decisions. KEY POINTS: Question LIBD has diverse etiologies and overlapping imaging patterns, but a practical, standardized radiological framework for differential diagnosis remains lacking. Findings This pictorial review summarizes characteristic CT/MRI findings of common LIBD-associated diseases and establishes a stepwise diagnostic approach integrating obstruction points, morphology, and clinical information. Critical Relevance Statement By combining specific imaging patterns with clinical context, this review provides a practical differential diagnostic framework that may improve diagnostic confidence, guide further evaluation, and facilitate earlier detection of malignant transformation in LIBD.
